title: Why Buffalo Bills Need to Keep Ian Wheeler over Veteran RB
full_text:
Since signing with the Buffalo Bills ahead of the 2023 season, Ty Johnson has proven to be a reliable backup, especially on third downs. In three seasons with the Bills, Johnson has 545 yards and four touchdowns as a runner, while averaging 4.5 yards per attempt.
As a receiver, he's hauled in 49 receptions for 609 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 12.4 yards per reception. Simply put, he's been an efficient back, but looking ahead to 2026, he shouldn't be a lock to make the 53-man roster.
Johnson, who will turn 29 in September, saw a decline in his numbers this past season. His rushing yards per attempt went down from 5.2 in 2024 to 4.0 in 2025. His yardage per reception dipped as well, with Johnson averaging 11.0 yards per catch, down from the 15.8 in 2025.
Those numbers aren't likely to increase this season for two reasons. One is his age, as most running backs begin to decline as they approach 30 years old. More importantly, offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael made it clear that Buffalo plans to use Cook as a receiver more often . Doing so will limit Johnson's snaps on third down, which is where he has done the majority of his damage.
If that truly is the plan, keeping Ian Wheeler over Johnson could make sense. Wheeler is a more traditional RB2 and has shown during the preseason that he has no issues making the most of every touch. We recently wrote about his jaw-dropping hit during Thursday's joint practce .
Against the Panthers, Wheeler ran for 41 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. This week, he added 56 yards on 14 attempts, plus another 21 yards on two receptions. That gives him 118 yards on 23 touches, for an average of 5.1 yards per touch. As a pure runner, Wheeler is averaging 4.6 yards per attempt.
Not only is Wheeler proving to be an effective player , but he also makes significantly less than Johnson. Wheeler, an undrafted free agent out of Howard, has a cap hit of $885,000 compared to $3.275 million for Johnson . Buffalo would save $2.455 million by moving on from Johnson, who has been dealing with a knee injury this offseason.
Another option could be placing Johnson on the short-term IR to begin the season, allowing him to get his knee fully healthy. That could also give Wheeler time to prove he belongs in the NFL, without the risk of losing Johnson.

title: Tyler Bass Restores Some Confidence vs. Browns, But Bills Aren't Out of the Woods Yet
full_text:
After not playing a snap last season due to injury, Buffalo Bills kicker Tyler Bass has been having an up-and-down offseason overall, but he managed to restore some confidence in the preseason Week 2 win over the Cleveland Browns.
After an ugly showing during practice on Thursday, when Bass missed two of his six field goal tries from 35 and 45 yards out, Buffalo's kicker drilled a 52-yarder on Saturday afternoon.
Bass also attempted four extra points, and he nailed all of them.
While the 52-yarder was certainly encouraging, especially given the elements he was battling, it is worth pointing out that Bass barely squeezed his lone field goal try through the upright.
Tyler Bass making it look easy from 52 yards! pic.twitter.com/eOQdgwvSpl
"He's got the right mentality," head coach Joe Brady said of Bass. "It was a lot of fun to watch. Got a lot of trust in him."
"Feels good, just kind of seeing all the hard work pay off," Bass said in the locker room after the game. It was a good situation for us and I'm glad we were able to go out there and execute."
"Going into my seventh year, so I've got some games under my belt, but it's just like a long-lost friend," Bass said when asked how it feels to be back. "You're just getting reacquainted to it and it feels good to be back and it's just a constant growth thing."
In all, Bass has made four of his five field goal tries in the preseason and all six of his extra points.
The duality of Bass has been on full display this offseason.
After missing a kick in preseason Week 1 , he appeared to have a strong practice last Tuesday, struggled on Thursday, and then turned it around on Saturday.
And, lest we forget, he wasn't exactly automatic before his injury after he posted back-to-back seasons in which he converted on 82.8% of his field goals following campaigns with 87.5% and 87.1% success rates.
Now, the Bills are hoping Bass can be reliable after not having played a single snap in the NFL since 2024. That might be a tall order, but at least he's moving in a positive direction after the second preseason game .
Bass will have more opportunities to get some work in at practice this week, and then he'll have one more dress rehearsal in the preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday.

title: Four Disappointments from Bills' Lopsided Win over Browns
full_text:
After a bit of a delayed start to the action due to a lightning delay at the beginning of the first quarter, the Buffalo Bills managed to come away with a dominating 31-7 victory over the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on Saturday afternoon to start the preseason 2-0 under first-year head coach Joe Brady .
Much like it did at the beginning of training camp at St. John Fisher University earlier this summer, the rain poured down sideways at times in Cleveland at the beginning of the exhibition contest before lightning ultimately forced an hour-long delay just under two minutes into the game.
Brady’s new mantra—”just put the ball down”—came in handy, though, as Buffalo came out swinging early and often the rest of the way in order to earn the convincing lopsided victory.
In a game where a team wins by 24 points , it can be hard to find any flaws.
But, if fans looked hard enough, there were still some noticeable warts that slightly marred the mostly sensational day from all three phases of the game.
Here are four disappointments in spite of the Bills remaining undefeated for the preseason.
For a second straight week, Buffalo’s rookie offensive tackle Jude Bowry struggled quite mightily during his time on the field.
The Bills only surrendered one sack during the game against the Browns on Saturday, but—just like last week against Carolina—it was Bowry who found himself on the losing end of the play.
The 2026 fourth-round pick out of Boston College is seemingly being counted on to be the swing tackle this upcoming regular season for Buffalo, so the fact that he’s had back-to-back preseason outings with notable struggles is quite concerning.
Maybe fellow offensive tackle Tylan Grable ends up stealing the job from the rookie before the preseason is over.
At first, the afternoon didn’t start out so hot for the Bills, particularly on defense.
In addition to the soggy conditions that mucked things up at the beginning, new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s unit had a bit of a slow start to the game as Buffalo surrendered a touchdown on Cleveland’s opening series with second-year quarterback Shadeur Sanders leading the way for the AFC North squad.
The Browns easily took the ball down the field 65 yards and capped off the drive with a passing touchdown from Sanders to wide receiver Luke Floriea, who found himself wide open at the back of the end zone on a 3rd-and-7 play from inside the red zone.
Overall, the defense did well to turn things around, especially when fellow Browns’ quarterback Deshaun Watson was in the game later on, but the early returns from that side of the ball weren’t pretty on Saturday.
It gave shades of Sean McDermott’s old “bend but don’t break” defense.
Of course, it was mostly backups on the field for the Bills, so it should be taken with a grain of salt, so to speak.
But, it was still disappointing to see, nonetheless.
Cleveland also matriculated the ball deep into Buffalo territory later on in the first half with Sanders, as well, but a bad pass from the young gunslinger bailed the defense out as the ball tipped up into the air and landed in the waiting arms of safety Damar Hamlin, who—in spite of the takeaway—mostly struggled in coverage for the duration of the day.
Misdirection on bootlegs seemed to be a big key for the Browns, so being disciplined and not overly aggressive will have to be a point of emphasis for Leonhard moving forward.
“Controlled chaos” needs to be the name of the game for this Bills’ defensive unit .
It wasn’t as many as last week, but once again the Bills found themselves snake bitten by penalties throughout the game, especially at inopportune times.
Whether it be an offsides penalty from rookie outside linebacker T.J. Parker on a third-and-long play that helped bail Cleveland’s offense out on one drive, or another silly offsides penalty at the end of the first quarter from fellow EDGE rusher Javon Solomon —when everyone on defense should've been aware of an incoming hard count—there were just too many undisciplined penalties from Buffalo once again on Saturday.
Last week versus the Panthers, the Bills had nine penalties for a total of 78 yards. Against the Browns? Buffalo committed six fouls for a total of 40 yards.
So, while the yardage may have gone down significantly, the number of infractions committed by the team this Saturday didn’t . . . at least not by much.
It’s not time to call Brady’s group undisciplined just yet, but it might be heading that way if this trend continues.
The goal should be less than five penalties from the team next week.
This final disappointment might seem a little strange to some fans, but it makes sense if you think about it from a big-picture perspective.
Buffalo still has several positional battles ongoing at the moment, and Saturday’s preseason outing against Cleveland didn’t really provide much clarity on any of them.
Rookie punter Tommy Doman Jr. and veteran Mitch Wishnowsky both were able to get punts off in the game, and Wishnowsky received the call for holding duties like Doman Jr. did last week against Carolina. Neither player did anything too overly positive or negative against the Browns to separate themselves further, which made the day a bit of a moot point.
Meanwhile, the competition along the starting defensive line between Landon Jackson and T.J. Sanders continues, as well as at left guard between Alec Anderson and Austin Corbett as each player saw time on the field against the Browns despite several other defensive and offensive starters sitting out for the matchup .
Jackson had a tackle for loss early in the game that was impressive, so maybe he slightly pulled away from Sanders, but the second-year player from South Carolina didn’t play too badly, either.
As for left guard, Anderson got the “start” amongst a bunch of backups.
Lastly, the battle between rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr and Dorian Williams doesn’t appear to be any closer to having a winner than it did before the game , either.
Overall, I guess that’s not totally a bad thing.
However, with roughly just a week remaining until final roster cuts have to be made on August 30, I’m sure general manager Brandon Beane and head coach Joe Brady would like a bit more clarity on some of the current competitions than they seem to have right now.
For that reason, it’s listed as a disappointment.

title: Bills’ Deone Walker Emerging as Three-Down Monster Thanks to Recent Weight Loss
full_text:
Buffalo Bills’ second-year defensive lineman Deone Walker silenced a lot of doubters during his rookie season.
Prior to being selected by Buffalo in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, the former University of Kentucky star had an up-and-down collegiate career that was marred by a pars defect—which is a small fracture between two vertebrae in the spine—that was quite debilitating for the now 22-year-old Detroit, Michigan, native.
He was still quite productive, though, and at times Walker was even thought to be a potential top-10 pick by some draft analysts during his time as an undergraduate at Kentucky.
But, then—somehow, some way—the one-time Cass Technical High School standout fell to the Bills at pick No. 109 in last year’s draft.
And, so far, it’s been a dream scenario for Buffalo while being a nightmare for the rest of the NFL, as Walker was named a member of the PFWA’s 2025 All-Rookie team last year after starting 16 of 17 games in the regular season en route to registering 39 total tackles, eight tackles for loss, four quarterback hits, and one sack.
He also added 6 tackles, two pass deflections, and one interception in Buffalo’s two postseason games this past January.
It was quite impressive, to say the least.
Now, however, it appears as if Walker is about to emerge into one of the NFL’s next great defensive superstars , especially after he dominated against the Carolina Panthers in Buffalo’s preseason opener on Saturday, August 15.
“It’s (all about) that comfortability of who you’re playing with,” Bills’ defensive lineman Deone Walker said to reporter Chris Brown on One Bills Live Friday afternoon ahead of Buffalo’s preseason game with the Cleveland Browns this weekend.
“I feel like, at least for me as a young guy—and I know a lot of my teammates feel the same way—we don’t care, young or not, can you make the plays that you need to make? If it’s the young guy, then it’s the young guy. If it’s the older guy, then it’s the older guy.
“Like, no matter what, (the) film shows it all.”
And, boy did it show recently against the Panthers.
In just 10 snaps of action, the young behemoth defensive lineman recorded three tackles, one sack, and one tackle for loss: it was scary . . . for Carolina and quarterback Bryce Young, at least.
As a whole, the Bills’ defense forced the Panthers’ starting offense to go three-and-out on its first three possessions of the game, and Walker was a major reason why.
And, since the preseason opener , many people can’t help themselves from thinking about all of the possibilities to come from the 6-foot-7, 331-pound defensive lineman in his sophomore NFL season this year. Even Walker appears to be ecstatic.
Well, not only is he excited for the shift to a 3-4 scheme under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard , but he’s also taken it upon himself this offseason to transform his body in order to—not only help alleviate any further possible back issues—but to also help give him a better chance to stay on the field more often.
Once listed at upwards of 345 pounds during his time as a Wildcat in college, Walker has trimmed down this training camp for the Bills in hopes of wreaking even more havoc in Western New York this fall and winter.
“I feel good, you know? (But), how do I look? Do I look good?” Walker jokingly continued in his most recent interview.
“It’s been great, you know? I feel way lighter . . . just trying to—what’s something else that I can do to help the team—you know? One of my big things (to work on) was wanting to be a three-down player. I want to be out there with Ed. I want to be out there with T.J. (on) those third-and-long situations.
“So, what can I do to better put myself into a position where they can’t tell me no, you know? So, (I’m) just going (into) every day trying to work.”
Thus far in training camp, it’s clear that he’s well on his way to doing so.
However, at this moment it’s unclear whether or not Walker and the rest of the defense will see much more action for the remainder of this preseason as first-year head coach Joe Brady has seemingly chosen to keep many of his plans close to the vest this summer.
But—even if they don’t—regardless of any downfalls from last year’s defense , the former all-rookie team member believes that this season will be special for him and his teammates on that side of the ball.
He’s certainly put in the work individually, and Walker’s ready to see it all come to fruition on the field starting this fall.
“It’s just football. At the end of the day, we know how to play football. Let’s go out there, have fun, and play,” Walker added.
“One thing, for us as a defensive line—d-line (and) OLBs—is (limiting) the penalties: the offsides, (and) the, you know, just those little ticky-tacky things that knock us off our game. (It’s about) just mitigating those. So, that’s our biggest thing. And, us just playing dominant as a whole group, you know? Our whole defensive front five, front four—whatever we’re in—just us dominating.
“We want to be able to take the game over with just us.”
If that were to happen, it could only mean good things for Buffalo this season.
We’ll soon find out what’s in store from Walker and Co., though, as the Bills’ season opener against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium on Sunday, September 13, is just three weeks away.
It won’t be long now, Bills Mafia .

title: Bills' Backup Quarterback Battle Catches Fire vs. Browns With Josh Allen Looking On
full_text:
Kyle Allen likely made viewers do a double take during the first half of the Buffalo Bills ' preseason road game against the Cleveland Browns on Saturday afternoon .
With franchise quarterback Josh Allen inactive per coach's decision , Kyle Allen got the first look in the Bills' backup quarterback competition . He took the starting snaps and accounted for a highly-efficient first half throwing the football.
"If I don't [play], I get to cheer on my guys, Kyle and Shane, going out there. Trying to be the best teammate I can be and give them anything that I can to help them out," said the five-time NFL MVP finalist Allen on Thursday.
On Saturday, the 30-year-old Kyle Allen, who is two months old than Josh, posted a 138.9 quarterback rating while averaging 10.7 yards per pass in the Bills' 31-7 road win .
After completing 10 of 12 pass attempts for 128 yards and one touchdown, Allen gave way to Shane Buechele at the start of the second half.
"Quarterbacks went out there, didn't blink," said rookie head coach Joe Brady . "It's raining during the National Anthem. I still called passes early. Hey, we gotta be able to throw the ball in the rain. How are we gonna be able to operate. It's like we've been doing in practice, so it was cool to see our quarterbacks at efficient football."
On the game-opening touchdown drive that was interrupted by a lightning delay, Allen went 2-of-2 passing for 35 yards. His two incompletions, both targeting tight end Jackson Hawes, were negated by defensive pass interference penalties.
"We got a lot of guys doing great things, receivers getting open for me, just playing within the system. Be prepared and just spread the ball around. It's been a good couple first games for offense all around," said Allen.
Kyle Allen throws a DIME for 37 yards 🎯 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZxND868Tyh
Just as he opened the first half, Allen closed it out with another touchdown drive. Running the two-minute offense to perfection, the Bills moved 62 yards on four consecutive pass completions in 47 seconds as a nine-yard strike to Mecole Hardman capped the scoring drive .
"I think I've slowly gotten better year over year for the past four or five years. It's tough to bounce around a bunch of places, but that's the job of a backup quarterback," said Allen.
Buechele, who has been a practice squad player for Buffalo, averaged 11.1 yards per attempt against the Browns. His quarterback rating came in at 123.3.
In addition to 5-of-10 passing for 111 yards and one touchdown, Buechele recorded a five-yard touchdown scramble on a 1st-and-goal play.
Shane Buechele said I GOT IT 😤 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fh6hQGedFf
Earlier in the second half, Buechele hit Ja'Mori Maclin in stride on a intermediate-range pass, and the receiver raced 71 yards on the touchdown reception .
"Getting the ball in the guys hands and key them do what they do. Guys were playing hard around us, so it's easy for us," said Buechele.

title: These Surprise Bills Player Helped Their Roster Chances With Strong Play Against Browns
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills improved to 2-0 on the preseason as they defeated the Cleveland Browns on the road in Week 2. It was a game that got off to a slow start after the two teams were forced to head to the locker room for roughly an hour due to a lightning delay.
Buffalo had to stop midway through their opening drive, but had no problem picking back up and scoring a touchdown to take a 7-0 lead. They struggled defensively on the opening drive, allowing Cleveland to tie it up at seven.
From there, it was all Buffalo as they wound up winning by a score of 31-7. Of course, the outcome in the preseason isn't the main focus. Instead, it's all about players fighting for a spot on the roster. That said, here's a look at every player who improved their odds of making the 53-man roster this weekend.
He was a stud in Week 1 against the Panthers, and that was the case once again in Week 2 against the Browns. Walker has been praised for his coverage, even recording a pick against Carolina.
This week, he showed he's willing to get physical as he delivered a hard hit on Raheim Sanders to force a fourth down on the opening drive. He still showed off his coverage skill, even recording a pass breakup to start the third quarter, knocking down a Deshaun Watson pass intended for Malachi Corley.
Trent Sherfield made an 18-yard reception right before the weather delay, but made sure to pick up where he left off once the teams were back on the field. Sherfield was targeted on the first snap following the delay, and again hauled it in, this time for a 17-yard gain. He finished with 54 yards on four receptions on four targets, making sure to put himself in play for a spot on the 53-man roster .
Ian Wheeler was one of the more impressive players on the field in Week 1 against the Panthers after rushing for 41 yards and a touchdown on seven attempts. This week, he was just as impressive, running hard while showing no hesitation to seek out contact. Wheeler ended his day with 56 yards on 14 carries. He also showed he can be a weapon in the passing game with 21 yards on two receptions.
Late in the first half, Ja'Mori Maclin caught a 37-yard pass that was a dime from Kyle Allen. This led to a touchdown right before the half, giving the Bills a 14-7 lead. After a Tyler Bass field goal, Maclin made another big play, catching a pass over the middle of the field from Shane Buechele and turning it into a 71-yard touchdown.
Shane Buechele finds Ja'Mori Maclin and he takes it 71 YARDS BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OKHXAspCQa
Kani Walker isn't the only defensive back who made noise on Saturday. Former UDFA Te'Cory Couch turned heads as well, recording three tackles and one pass breakup. What really stood out, however, was his leaping interception off Deshaun Watson in the third quarter. The Bills don't have elite depth at cornerback, which is why players such as Walker and Couch have hope following their showing this preseason.
Ian Wheeler wasn't the only running back who impressed in this one, with Frank Gore Jr. also standing out. Gore showed off his speed and quick burst, ripping off an 11-yard run followed by an 18-yarder in the third quarter. Gore finished with 54 yards on nine attempts. It won't be easy for either Wheeler or Gore to make Buffalo's roster, but they're both making it difficult to waive them.

title: Five Winners, Three Losers from Bills' Preseason Week 2 Win vs. Browns
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were in Northeast Ohio on Saturday to take on the Cleveland Browns in Week 2 of the NFL preseason. The game got off to an interesting start as the Bills moved into Cleveland territory in a hurry after Trent Sherfield hauled in an 18-yard reception at the Browns' 41.
As soon as that play ended, both teams had to exit the field when play was stopped due to a lightning delay . The game wound up resuming around 2:15 p.m. and the Bills finished the drive with a one-yard touchdown run from Ray Davis, who scored one hour and nine minutes after their drive began.
Cleveland answered quickly, but then it was a lopsided affair with Buffalo winning 31-7. With this game behind us, here's a look at which players stood out as both winners and losers.
Wide receiver is a deep position for the Bills, with the first five spots seemingly locked up. That means multiple players are fighting for the sixth spot, assuming Buffalo goes that deep. If they do, Trent Sherfield is ensuring his name is in the mix.
The veteran wideout is in his second stint with the team and has been making waves during camp and that carried into this game. Sherfield hauled in two passes on the opening drive, gaining 35 yards as he helped the Bills get into range for the opening-drive touchdown.
Following a long opening drive, the Bills were on the field for just three plays on the second drive. It was an ugly drive that was derailed when Mike Hall beat rookie offensive tackle Jude Bowry on a speed rush. Hall moved past Bowry easily, sacking Kyle Allen for a nine-yard loss. That put Buffalo in a third-and-17 situation, unsurprisingly leading to a punt two plays later.
Buffalo used a fourth-round pick on Bowry, hoping he could provide depth behind starters Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown. With the regular season quickly approaching, it's clear that he's not ready for the swing tackle role. There's no reason to panic because he can still develop into a quality player, but the Bills need to lean on someone else if one of their starters goes down.
The Bills' defense was struggling throughout the first half and it looked as though they were going to allow Cleveland to take the lead late in the second half. Shedeur Sanders was leading them on a long drive and was finding open players with ease, sitting at 8-for-8 on the day. Sanders finally made a mistake, however, and the duo of Joe Andreessen and Damar Hamlin made him pay.
On the eighth play of the long drive, Sanders' pass was slightly behind tight end Jermaine Terry, and Andreessen tipped it into the air. He was credited with a pass defense , which allowed Hamlin to record an interception. It was the first incompletion of the day for Sanders and the first time the defense had something to get fired up over.
Damar Hamlin comes up with the INT 🙌 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SBow1PXq6x
Andreessen continued to step up after this as he played with plenty of energy. The fan favorite finished with four tackles, but was all over the field, so it felt like much more than that.
While Trent Sherfield was making a case for a spot on the 53-man roster, Mecole Hardman Jr. made it tougher on himself. Hardman's path to the team was always going to be as a return man, but the Bills still need him to contribute on offense. They tried to get him involved in this one and Hardman struggled with two drops in the first half. The second was on third-and-three and led to their third consecutive punt.
Hardman responded nicely, recording a touchdown on a screen play on the following drive, giving his team a 14-7 lead. That said, the fact that he was on the field with players not expected to make the team, coupled with his drops, won't help his chances of making the team.
Buffalo's defense made life miserable for Deshaun Watson, holding him to 35 yards on 5-of-12 passing. They also had an interception, which was an impressive grab from Te'Cory Couch.
Te'Cory Couch with the INT! BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UQXxepOOG7
Couch showed excellent awareness to bring that pass in. The ball was overthrown by Watson and Couch had multiple players around him and the ball got to him in a hurry. Still, he got both of his hands around it and held on as he hit the ground.
It wasn't too long ago when there were concerns surrounding Kyle Allen as the backup. After two preseason games, Allen has been impressive and quieted the noise. This weekend, he was especially impressive, going 10-of-12 for 128 yards with a touchdown. He had several impressive throws, including a 37-yarder to Ja'Mori Maclin on their scoring drive just before halftime.
The opening drive was ugly for the Bills entire defensive line. They were struggling to get any pressure, especially on key third down plays . While several players could have been pointed to, it was especially concerning for DeWayne Carter. After missing the 2025 season, Carter bulked up to fit Jim Leonhard's scheme. On Saturday, he was unable to make much of an impact and had a tough time getting off blocks. With Buffalo recently adding Greg Gaines, Carter is on the bubble and didn't help himself out against the Browns. It also wasn't a great sign for Carter that he was on the field in the fourth quarter, which suggests his spot might not be safe.
Buffalo put this one away before the fourth quarter, thanks to Ja'Mori Maclin. The undrafted free agent from Kentucky took a pass from Shane Buechele and turned it into a massive gain. Maclin made defenders miss as he turned upfield for a 71-yard touchdown, giving the Bills a 24-7 lead.
Shane Buechele finds Ja'Mori Maclin and he takes it 71 YARDS BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OKHXAspCQa
That was his second big catch of the game as Maclin also came down with a 37-yarder from Kyle Allen just before the half. That helped move the chains on their scoring drive late in the second quarter.

title: Joe Brady's Prudent Choice Sitting Bills' Key Veterans vs. Browns in Delayed Game
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' first-year head coach Joe Brady apparently saw enough during Thursday's joint practice on the road against the Cleveland Browns.
After the Bills' first-teamers made their presence felt on the practice field, a number of the veteran starters are watching the August 22 preseason game from the sideline.
"I told the team, I want to see how today's practice goes. Ideal world, a lot of the 1s would, hey, we get a great day's practice today, and we kind of go from there and I feel like they got the work they needed," said Brady prior to the August 20 joint session.
Franchise quarterback Josh Allen, who started the August 15 preseason opener by engineering back-to-back scoring drives, isn't getting any snaps against the Browns on Saturday in Cleveland. The five-time NFL MVP finalist looked fabulous spinning the football around the yard on Thursday by multiple accounts.
The Bills also held out offensive line starters left tackle Dion Dawkins, right tackle Spencer Brown, right guard O'Cyrus Torrence and center Connor McGovern, who has been out since August 8 due to injury . Notably, veteran center Lloyd Cushenberry, who started in place of McGovern last week, was also given the day off.
Buffalo tight ends Dawson Knox and Dalton Kincaid along with RB1 James Cook and WR1 DJ Moore remained on the sideline when the starting offense took the field.
Running back Ray Davis earned the start and opened the game with an eight-yard gain.
After four snaps, the game was delayed due to lightning in the area . Only 1:49 came off the first-quarter clock prior to referee Bill Vinovich sending both teams to the locker room.
Prior to the Bills' pregame warmups, multiple first-team defensive players were seen working out. That routine usually signals that those men won't see game action. Cornerback Christian Benford, safety Cole Bishop, edge rusher Greg Rousseau, nose tackle Deone Walker and edge rusher Michael Hoecht were in that group.
Wide receivers Khalil Shakir, Skyler Bell and Dante Pettis are all dealing with undisclosed lower body injuries, although none appear to be severe.
All three wide receivers went through on-field work with trainers prior to Saturday's game. The aforementioned McGovern and fifth-round rookie safety Jalon Kilgore were also involved. Veteran safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was spotted on a stationary bicycle.
The Bills gave Alec Anderson the start at left guard as he battles against veteran Austin Corbett for first-team status.
Meanwhile, the rest of the starting line was comprised entirely of reserves with left tackle Tylan Grable, center Sedrick Van Pran Granger, rookie right guard Armaj Reed-Adams and fourth-round right tackle Jude Bowry.
With Kyle Allen getting the start, Shane Buechele is most likely set to play the second half as the Bills attempt to identify the best backup option .
The good news is that Josh Allen will get to spend the day with a clipboard. There's simply no benefit to exposing the franchise field general in a road exhibition. Had the game been at home, one could argue that Allen should take the opportunity to continue to become acclimated in the new stadium.
"Whatever Coach asks me to do. Obviously, whether I play or not, I'm going to be happy with the decision," said the five-time NFL MVP finalist Allen. "If I don't [play], I get to cheer on my guys, Kyle and Shane, going out there. Trying to be the best teammate I can be and give them anything that I can to help them out."

title: The Biggest Concern for Panthers in 2026 Isn't Bryce Young
full_text:
This Friday evening, the reigning NFC South champions will wrap up their four-game preseason by hosting the Houston Texans. The club owns a 2-1 record this summer, somewhat notable considering the team owned a combined 1-8 preseason mark the previous three years.
Late last week and prior to Carolina Panthers’ 34-17 victory at Jacksonville last Friday, Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus identified the biggest concern for each of the league’s 32 teams entering the start of the upcoming season. For Canales’s squad, it’s a pretty obvious choice that team has hopefully found the solution to.
“The Panthers are currently without both starting offensive tackles ” explained McGuinness. “Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon in the wild-card loss to the Rams, while right tackle Taylor Moton is sidelined with blood clots. It remains unclear when either will return in 2026, but both appear likely to miss at least the start of the season.
Each of these blockers could be considered mainstays since joining the organizations. Ekwonu was the sixth overall pick in the 2022 draft from North Carolina State. He has played and started 65 out of a possible 69 games, including the aforementioned playoff clash with Sean McVay’s team.
Meanwhile, Moton was a second-round selection back in 2017 from Western Michigan. He played in all 16 regular-season contests and a postseason games as a rookie without a start. Since 2018, he has been in the opening lineup in 129 of the club’s 130 total outings. While Ekwonu’s availability has obviously been a question mark since mid-January, Moton’s medical concerns were revealed in June.
In any case, Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan was already looking ahead this offseason when it came to the left tackle issue. He added four-year pro Rasheed Walker (Packers) in free agency, and used the 19th overall selection in April’s draft on University of Georgia standout Monroe Freeling.
“Walker earned a 69.3 PFF pass-blocking grade in 2025,” added McGuinness, “while Freeling was one of college football’s top pass protectors, allowing just two pressures on 469 pass-blocking snaps. Still, losing both starting tackles is a significant concern, and for all of Freeling’s potential, he has yet to play an NFL snap.”
Yes, I understand this was against the Jags 2s. Still, love seeing that right side of Robert Hunt, Monroe Freeling, and Tommy Tremble parting the seas for Jonathon Brooks. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/YgeLNjH8AP
To be clear, the former Bulldog did not play vs. the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame Game, but did log 10 offensive snaps in the team’s preseason loss at Buffalo. Freeling was back in the starting lineup vs. Jacksonville, playing 13 offensive snaps, as well as one on special teams.
Hence, as it stands at the moment, Panthers’ quarterback Bryce Young will be playing behind a vastly-different offensive front early in the season —which includes a new face at center as well—than he lined up with over his first three years with the franchise.

title: Could Haynes King Push Bryce Young for Panthers' QB1 Spot?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are not entertaining a camp battle at quarterback . They're all in on Bryce Young for now . But if we're all being honest, there's been one quarterback who has looked the best this preseason, and it's UDFA Haynes King .
They've all played varying sample sizes and against varying levels of competition, but if we're strictly evaluating how they played in a vacuum, then King has outdone Young, Kenny Pickett, and Kyle Trask, none of whom have particularly struggled.
Could King ever push the Panthers, who don't yet have an answer at quarterback beyond 2027, Young's option year, to start?
It was against the backups (and backups of the backups, to be truthful) for a team projected to nab the number one overall pick in the next draft, but Haynes King was electric in the Hall of Fame Game. And good football is good football.
We all began to fantasize about King's career that night. What could he be? Could the Panthers have found a true diamond in the rough? Couple that with a partly inauspicious preseason for Bryce Young, and there are legitimately some people wondering if the Panthers might be better off with King under center.
But, to be blunt, there's almost no chance King ever becomes a starting quarterback in the NFL. There have been five UDFA QBs who have gone on to be multi-year starters: Tony Romo, Warren Moon, Jeff Garcia, Dave Krieg, and Kurt Warner.
That's a good group of quarterbacks, but the odds are not in King's favor of joining them. There are a handful of undrafted quarterbacks every single year, and only five have ever been notable enough to start more than one season.
What King could do is become a good backup quarterback, and we believe that's his trajectory. It's a shame he has not been on the field since that Hall of Fame Game, but he showed enough to suggest that he could overtake Kenny Pickett, who's also been solid this preseason, as the primary backup.
The Panthers aren't, nor should they be, considering starting anyone else besides Young this year. That's partly because he's earned it and partly because it's pretty much the final year for evaluating the fourth-year QB.
But the Panthers do have an opportunity with King, even if he never starts. He could be a gadget player or a QB sneak option, as well as a good backup.
The Panthers have to roster him, though. They can't afford to lose King to another team if he lands on the practice squad, so they have to roster him. Then they can use him as the primary backup if he outplays Pickett or in 2027, when Pickett hits free agency.
No, King isn't better than nor should he start over Young, but he absolutely deserves a spot on the roster.

title: Panthers Have Not Given Bryce Young What He Needs in Make-or-Break Year 4
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have tried to support Bryce Young , especially once it became clear that he could not overcome an abysmal roster in 2023. They began adding pieces at various spots on offense to try to help. Unfortunately, in 2026, it's clear that it didn't work very well.
The first thing a team can do for its quarterback is give him weapons to throw to. The Panthers have done a passable job of that, but we can't pretend this pass-catching unit is elite. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker are doing all the heavy lifting.
PFF ranked them 22nd in the NFL , and it's hard to disagree with the ranking. There aren't 22 better duos in the NFL than McMillan and Coker, but there are so many other players to consider, and for the Panthers, most of them are simply not very good.
"Beyond those two, there is very little proven talent to speak of in this receiving room. Tight ends Ja’Tavion Sanders and Tommy Tremble have combined for four straight PFF receiving grades in the 50.0s over the last two seasons," the blurb for the Panthers read.
The second thing a team can do for its quarterback is provide him with a good running game. The Panthers have tried to do that and probably believe that they have, but the numbers disagree. Even with Rico Dowdle last year, the running game was not good.
This year, PFF ranked them 27th , and it's once again hard to disagree. None of Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne, or AJ Dillon has the explosiveness needed to really succeed in the NFL. Jonathon Brooks might, but he's a wild card.
"Question marks remain over the health of Jonathon Brooks, who has taken just nine handoffs since he was drafted 46th overall two years ago," the blurb read.
The final thing a team can do for its quarterback is protect him. The Panthers have done a better job of protecting Bryce Young than providing him weapons or a running game, but it's still not a good situation thanks to injuries.
In fact, PFF rightly noted that the Panthers' offensive line is a top-five unit most primed for regression. The line was very good in 2025, but it could be rough in 2026. There are a lot of talented players, but how well do they fit?
Some key losses, both injury-related and other, have tanked this line. Ikem Ekwonu, Taylor Moton, Austin Corbett, and Cade Mays, all of whom posted 66.0 or better PFF grades, are gone for right now.
"Ekwonu is expected to miss the majority of the season after suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in the playoffs, while Moton will be sidelined into the starting slate due to blood clots in his lung. Also, former starting center Cade Mays headed to Detroit, while Corbett is now in Buffalo," PFF analyst Bradley Locker wrote.
Locker noted that the Panthers added nice replacements in Monroe Freeling, Rasheed Walker, Sam Hecht, and Luke Fortner, but that's a lot of new additions to the line, and there's no telling how rookies Freeling and Hecht will fare in their first NFL seasons.
Simply put, the Panthers have tried and failed to surround Bryce Young with help. This is probably the best overall offense he's had in the NFL, but the bar is on the floor, and even with the talent they do have, there are major question marks.

title: Jonathon Brooks' Biggest Issue in Preseason Week 2 Could Limit Snaps With Panthers
full_text:
Running back Jonathon Brooks had a few standout moments in the Carolina Panthers' preseason Week 2 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, but it wasn't all good for him.
Brooks ripped off an 11-yard run during the contest, and he was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his career on a one-yard carry in the first quarter.
However, Brooks' pass-blocking left a lot to be desired. Brooks saw three pass-blocking reps, according to Pro Football Focus , and gave up two pressures and scored a putrid 6.6 grade.
Here's one of those snaps in which he gave up a pressure.
Jonathon Brooks has to be better in pass pro here. Bad whiff. This is likely a first down for Brycen Tremayne if Brooks does his job. Have to be better in this area if you're going to be reliable on third downs. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/wN2i57dpWn
Now, to be fair, Brooks did redeem himself in another pass pro rep later on, but his showing overall was not good.
It goes without saying that Bryce Young's life is going to be a lot harder if his running backs can't adequately block for him.
We saw that first hand in the clip above, as Young's throw was clearly impacted on a play that otherwise would have gained yardage if Young had a cleaner look.
More specifically for Brooks, he can't hope to see many snaps on third downs if his pass pro isn't up to snuff. If he doesn't improve, Brooks is going to cede even more work to Chuba Hubbard, who remains the favorite to lead the backfield at the start of the year, and quite possibly even Trevor Etienne or AJ Dillon.
PFF has charted four pass-blocking snaps in total for Brooks in the preseason. The third-year back had a successful rep in the previous preseason game, and had another in the second.
That said, the bad has been really bad thus far.
The good news for Brooks is that Etienne hasn't been much better with his pass pro snaps. Etienne has registered a 29.1 grade in two pass protection snaps this preseason, and he posted a 22.9 grade through three pass-blocking snaps last season.
Hubbard is the best and most proven blocker of the trio, but he isn't great in that area by any stretch after posting a lackluster grade of 46.8 in 2025.
All of this points to a pass protection problem in the backfield for the Panthers, and it's one they need to fix.
Outside of the clear struggles in pass protection, Brooks took a step forward in his second preseason game of the season.
He barely averaged three yards per carry and only finished with five carries for 18 yards, but those were still better numbers than last week. He also ripped off an 11-yard run when the right side of Carolina's offensive line opened up a nice hole for him.
That run, along with his score, will only help Brooks build confidence as the regular season approaches.

title: Carolina Panthers' Costly Offensive Line at Risk of Major Regression Soon
full_text:
The theme of the Carolina Panthers ' offseason has been change. Spending heavily in free agency , the Panthers entered training camp having spent the fifth-most money in the league on contracts.
Not only did Carolina make huge changes on defense, but on the offensive line, new faces are all over the line now and look to prove themselves on short-term deals.
As far as free agency goes, Carolina signed two new faces to the line. Rasheed Walker at left tackle, leaving Green Bay for Carolina, and Luke Fortner from the division rival Saints. The Panthers also used the 19th pick in the NFL Draft on Monroe Freeling, out of Georgia.
A revamped offensive line isn't always a positive. If anything, this unit only has more question marks than answers heading into the season.
PFF's Bradley Locker dropped his predictions for the five units in the NFL that could regress in 2026 on Thursday. On that list, the Panthers' offensive line, and rightfully so. The line is revamped, but while fresh faces can be a good thing, key starters from last season's 8th-ranked offensive line won't be on the field.
Including playoffs, Cade Mays started at center for the Panthers in 13 games. Since the Wild Card loss, Mays has departed Carolina, signing with the Detroit Lions. In the regular season, Mays logged 726 snaps and allowed 0 sacks.
Luke Fortner replaces Mays, a solid, experienced starter who played for the New Orleans Saints and Jacksonville Jaguars. Fortner posted a 72.5 PFF pass-blocking grade. That's the seventh-highest in the NFL for centers who qualify.
Taylor Moton was set to start at right tackle in 2026, but is currently dealing with blood clots . Moton is being replaced by a rookie to start the year. Monroe Freeling does have absurd upside and was selected in the first round. Rookie linemen usually have growing pains, and Freeling was supposed to be the backup left tackle.
The one silver lining is that Freeling has experience at right tackle, logging snaps there in his junior year. Freeling has also been open and honest about not caring where he plays; this was evident at the NFL Combine, when he took snaps at center.
Then theres new personnel at left tackle as well; Rasheed Walker takes over starting duties. Walker wouldn't have been needed if Ikem Ekwonu wasn't injured, though. Ekwonu will likely miss the entire 2026 season due to a torn patellar tendon suffered in the Wild Card loss against the Rams.
Playing 942 snaps in 2025, Ekwonu only gave up 5 sacks in the season. Now, in his first year in a new system, Walker is supposed to be a stable, and reliable piece of this pass protection, especially as he fights for a long-term deal, whether it's in Carolina or not.
Continuity is key for a successful offensive line. Carolina has clearly lost that to begin the 2026 NFL season. In the last two years, the Panthers are 0-2 to begin the season; that trend may very well continue if this unit struggles to gel out of the gate.
$102.3 million, thats how expensive the Panthers' offensive line is in 2026. Spending over 30% of the salary cap space on a unit means it needs to be not just good, but consistently good.
Carolina has multiple players who have just one year left on their deals, including Ekwonu, who is making a lofty $17.56 million this season whilst recovering from injury.
Regression up front also means regression from Bryce Young, who enters a pivotal contract season and is under more pressure than almost any other QB in the NFL. The last thing that the Panthers want to do is make any drastic moves. Now it's up to both Young and the trenches up front to step forward.

title: Carolina Panthers Crushed Jaguars, But Here's What Really Matters
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers easily handled the Jacksonville Jaguars in their third preseason outing to move to 2-1. Ordinarily, that result alone would be a good thing. But in the preseason, wins and losses don't matter, even if the Panthers happen to seemingly dominate. Here's what does matter, though.
Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan were a great duo last season. They terrorized the Jaguars in joint practice. They did it again in very sparse action in this contest, drawing a clear pass interference for a first down and making another big gain with McMillan working out of the slot. That gives the Panthers some interesting wrinkles to work with, especially after Chris Brazzell's injury.
We didn't expect AJ Dillon to make the roster, and he still might not. But he is making that a very hard decision to make. Trevor Etienne plays special teams, and that matters, but Dillon has been a force on the ground. He's been downright excellent as a backup, looking perhaps the best of all three main backs. He has potentially forced his way onto the roster, which is a huge achievement.
There was plenty of concern over last week's poor offensive showing sans Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt. If that had continued with them back in the lineup, there would be some major offensive problems. Fortunately, with them back, the offense ran much smoother. Protection was still an issue, but it was much better, especially in the middle.
the Panthers starting LB2 is not on the roster
The Panthers are having an LB2 competition between Claudin Cherilus and Trevin Wallace, and really, anyone could put their name in the ring. It's that open a competition. Tonight, without Devin Lloyd, was a good chance to analyze the contenders, and they were pretty much all bad. The Panthers don't need an ace linebacker there, but they don't have a starting-caliber player.
Does it really matter if the Panthers have several players capable of being a WR4-6? Not really, because NFL offenses don't use them like that. Still, Jimmy Horn and John Metchie have looked very solid as special teamers and on offense, and Ja'seem Reed didn't play, but he's been great, too. There's some depth at the back end.

title: Grading Bryce Young and Other Panthers QBs in Preseason Contest vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Preseason game No. 3 is in the books , and the Carolina Panthers looked better than ever on the road in Jacksonville. While half of Carolina's four touchdowns were on the ground, the quarterback play looked like a whole new unit compared to the road preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills .
In a dominant 34-17 win over the Jaguars, three QBs saw the field, and each of them was able to be productive and make impressive plays. None of Carolina's QBs made any catastrophic plays that resulted in turnovers.
The snap count for each QB wasn't very even, but all three put enough on film to earn grades. Here's how Bryce Young, Kenny Pickett, and Kyle Trask performed under the friday night lights in Jacksonville
Throwing just six passes, Young made the most of his limited action in Jacksonville. Young finished the game completing 5 of 6 pass attempts, totaling 49 yards.
Carolina's first drive wasn't pretty at all, but it was primarily because the pass protection was lacking. Young didn't panic with pressure coming his way, and made up for it on the second drive.
Carolina's franchise QB showed a little bit of everything: patience in the pocket before finding Tetairoa McMillan, scrambling away from defenders, and completing a short pass on the sideline.
Young found both Coker and McMillan, which is key as they build more chemistry heading into the 2026 season. McMillan almost scored a touchdown off a short pass from Young but was stopped at the one yard line.
Desicion making looked on point, and Young was able to be consistent and lead the Panthers down the field for what turned into a Jonathon Brooks 1-yard rushing touchdown.
It's important to note that Young and the first team offense played against the Jaguars second team defense, but that just means Young did was he was supposed to do.
Seeing the most game action of any Panthers QB. Pickett had some ups and downs early in the second quarter, but tightened up and led Carolina into multiple scoring drives.
Pickett finished the night 15/25, for 137 passing yards and a beautiful touchdown pass to Roc Taylor. Carolina's clear QB2's passer rating improved throughout the night, finishing at an 88.2.
60% completion percentage isn't anything to write home about, but Pickett was decisive and made plays when needed.
Pickett's connection with John Metchie III was the highlight of the night. The two connected on multiple chunk plays, and Metchie ended the night with 6 catches for 77 yards, leading Carolina.
Trask is the newest QB on the roster, being brought in after undrafted free agent Haynes King hurt his hamstring.
Trask did a lot of handing off the ball, but he completed all 4 of his passes for 52 yards and even threw a touchdown pass to Casey Washington. One play that stood out was also to Washington, where Trask rolled out to his right and completed a pass on the move for a first down.
Not much to grade, but nothing negative to takaway from Trask's performance either.

title: Major Takeaways from Carolina Panthers' Enormous Preseason Win vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Preseason games don't matter, and they certainly don't matter when teams use their starters versus backups. A lot of Carolina Panthers starters played, while plenty of Jacksonville Jaguars did not. Still, positive reps are positive reps, and negative reps are negative. Here's what we learned.
The Panthers opened up with a much better first drive, but it ended the same: with a punt. The reason? Pressure on every single passing play. Bryce Young avoided a couple of sacks with some nice movement, otherwise it would have been a truly ugly series once again. That has to get cleaned up.
Ironically, despite poor pass protection again, Bryce Young looked quite comfortable out there. He navigated the pocket really well to avoid the pressure, and his chemistry with the receivers was very solid. It was a very solid performance for the fourth-year QB, an encouraging sign after a lackluster preseason debut last week. He and Tetairoa McMillan picked up right where they left off in joint practice.
Travis Hunter, Trevor Lawrence, and other Jaguars starters didn't play, but some of the same secondary issues still cropped up. The zone scheme left some players wide open again, and even when they were covered, the Panthers struggled to make plays on the ball with their top defenders, most notably Mike Jackson, who has not had a great preseason. C.J. Williams gave the Panthers fits.
Princely Umanmielen made a great case to start last week opposite Jaelan Phillips. This week, without Phillips, he was a pest in the backfield once again. Pat Jones got a sack early on, but Umanmielen had multiple pressures and looked to be just as unblockable. He really might force the Panthers to put him on the field early and often this year.
I don’t think Jimmy Horn Jr. should be considered to be in a #Panthers roster battle with John Metchie, David Moore and/or Brycen Tremayne anymore Return value. WR value. Run blocking on the AJD tuddy. Hell, he was lead block on the kick return right before halftime.
What are the Panthers going to do with the final few WRs? Jimmy Horn Jr. is making his claim to be on the roster. He hasn't been exceptional as a receiver, but he's been very solid on special teams. That continued today, and he had a really good run on a trick play, which could be his role as it was last year.
The Panthers have a difficult decision on their hands. If we assume they're keeping three running backs, things are going to be tough. Trevor Etienne is good on special teams and as a receiver, but AJ Dillon has been very good this preseason, driving through contact and creating extra yards. It's going to comw down to the wire between those two behind Jonathon Brooks and Chuba Hubbard.
One of the things that kept a mediocre defense afloat last year an opportunistic streak. They forced a lot of turnovers. This year, they have the talent to survive without that, but it would still be good. In tonight's game, they forced two turnovers, the first two of the preseason. Chau Smith-Wade intercepted a pass and Cam Gill recovered a fumble forced by DeVonta Smith.

title: 7 Players to Watch While Panthers Look to Right Ship vs. Jaguars
full_text:
Tonight, the Carolina Panthers are taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars, and all eyes will be on Carolina after an underwhelming, to put it lightly, showing against the Buffalo Bills. Almost everyone needs to play better, but there are a few players we're watching closely to see how they do this week.
We were willing to give Bryce Young a pass for an inauspicious start to the preseason . The fourth-year QB has been great in camp, and the protection was abysmal during his nine snaps in the preseason. With his starting guards back, he should be better. Regardless, he needs to show something more, even if the cards are stacked against him.
Speaking of, both Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt are expected to play tonight. That's a huge development. Mostly, we're looking to see if the protection improves. There are some new pieces up front, but not these two. If their presence can stabilize things, great. If they can't, then this offensive line (and offense as a whole) is in big trouble.
So far, there's been no conversation about Pat Jones not starting. He is expected to return tonight after an injury absence and start opposite Jaelan Phillips. If he doesn't produce, those conversations might begin to crop up, especially since the Phillips-Princely Umanmielen pairing was absolutely electric last week against the Buffalo Bills.
This goes for Jaycee Horn as well, but we're not as concerned about him. Last week, Mike Jackson was beat in coverage plenty of times, as wide receivers were routinely wide open. The zone scheme doesn't seem to help, but he thrived in it in 2025. He and the team need Jackson to perform, as he's angling for a contract and the Panthers want to have success on the back end.
Monroe Freeling only played 10 snaps, so take this with a grain of salt, but he was not good last week. He posted a sub-40.0 PFF pass protection grade, though his run-blocking was fairly decent. That's got to improve. Freeling is the protector of the future, and the Panthers took a risk selecting him (one that has paid off with Taylor Moton's injury, but still), and he needs to prove himself.
It was impossible to get a read on the Panthers' first-team WRs last week because no one on offense made an impact in nine plays. But we know what Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker bring to the table. It's Xavier Legette who remains a wild card. What he does after a solid camp will be very telling.

title: Mike Jackson Will Get Paid; Should Panthers Foot the Expensive Bill?
full_text:
When the Carolina Panthers are through with the 2026 season, one of their biggest offseason decisions will be at cornerback, where the team will have to decide on what to do with Mike Jackson, who is entering the final year of his deal.
Initially signed to a cheap one-year deal in 2024, Jackson was re-signed on a two-year, $10.5 million contract in 2025 and went on to have a sensational season.
According to Pro Football Focus , Jackson's 80.9 coverage grade was third among all cornerbacks, and he gave up a completion rate of 55.6% and a passer rating of 72.9.
PFF also recently noted that Jackson is the 10th-highest graded player from 2025 who is entering a contract year in 2026.
On the surface, it would seem like paying Jackson to keep him around for the long haul is an easy decision, but that is not the case.
As great as Jackson was last season , there is no world in which the Panthers should unload a lot of money on him, especially before this season plays out.
After all, there's no telling if last season was a fluke and if Jackson will return to the lackluster form we saw in 2024.
Even if Jackson plays 2026 out and goes on to have yet another strong showing, the Panthers still should not be backing up the Brinks truck for him.
That's because Jackson is set to turn 30 in January and we all know that's the age when many players begin to decline.
The Panthers simply can't risk giving Jackson a lucrative, long-term deal, only to have his play significantly decline at the beginning or during the middle of his new deal.
Now, none of this is to say the Panthers shouldn't re-sign Jackson at all. If Carolina can get the veteran cornerback on a short-term deal that provides a reasonable bump in pay, it's worth keeping him around because finding a replacement could become expensive giving the rising cost of cornerbacks.
Spotrac estimates a three-year, $40 million deal for Jackson in his next contract. That amounts to about $13 million annually, which isn't bad but is still a bit too rich for our blood.
We'd be more comfortable in the range of a two-year, $20 million deal that doesn't have much, if any, commitment in the second year. That would amount to nearly double the previous deal Jackson received from Carolina.

title: The Key Questions for Chicago Bears Coming Out of Loss to Bengals
full_text:
Every game in the NFL produces answers, and those answers lead to more questions.
Even preseason games, like Saturday's 27-9 Bears loss to Cincinnati, follow this pattern. The questions might even be more numerous because it is only preseason.
It might be what happened in the game or even before it, but there were more questions arising from the Bengals-Bears game and practice, carrying over to this week's Titans practice and game.
Here are seven big question to come out of a Bears loss at Cincinnati.
Bears will never be a superbowl contending team until Poles gets the DL, primarily the pass rush right.
Although they used starters against the Bengals, one of their starting edge players didn't play at all. Dayo Odeyingbo was in for 16 snaps coming back from Achilles surgery, six more than Montez Sweat. Yet, Booker didn't suit up and hadn't been listed with any injured players.
The Bears need Booker healthy badly for the start of the season. They can't stand to have  the same thing happen that happened last year, when he was injured on special teams in a preseason game and missed half the schedule. Then again, if Booker isn't hurt, then why rest him when they're playing Montez Sweat?
I don’t care that Grady Jarrett is a tenured vet. Put him in the game and let him hurt someone on the other team
Apparently he ranks behind Cam Lewis in the safety pecking order because they started Lewis and then brought in Woods.
Eventually, Woods finished with 14 reps on defense. Woods, who is 31, has played over 6,800 snaps at safety in his career. Lewis has been a slot cornerback as much as he has been a safety, and has been a sub as often as he has been a starter.
Are the Bears unhappy with what they've had from Woods?
Not seeing much on film w/ the Xavier Woods injury. 3 plays before he left the game, he chased down Dylan Sampson on a screen. He appeared to briefly motion down the #Bears sideline after the play, but he stayed in on the next 2 plays and appeared to be moving fine. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/JzjLrD6scS
He signed on Aug. 17. Ben Johnson said he would need to be ramped up a bit to start practicing. It's almost a week and he hasn't been involved in practice and certainly didn't play. Did he injure himself signing the contract? Ogunjobi signed and failed a physical, then never played for the Bears.
Maybe Davenport just requires a bigger ramp based on all of his past injuries?
Grady Jarrett and Marcus Davenport on my DLine pic.twitter.com/mglnpWoCXN
When the Bears reported for camp, GM Ryan Poles was re-assuring everyone about some injuries.
Poles said Elijah Hicks, their backup safety to Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman, had an injury.
"Elijah Hicks has some discomfort in his shin; we got that taken care of," Poles said. "So that’s going to take a little bit of time, but he’s on the mend, he’s walking around; we don’t see that as anything major."
Hicks hasn't been taken off of the PUP list.
Poles also said something else, this about rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott.
"Keyshaun Elliott has some discomfort in his back; we took care of that," Poles said of their fifth-round pick. "He’s in really good shape, if you saw him walking around you would have no idea — he’s running. Obviously, there’s return-to-play protocol where you’re getting back to being a football player in terms of your strength, your conditioning, so he’ll be in that.
The two players they "took care of" still haven't practiced almost a month later.
Who else did they "take care of" and who's doing the taking care?
Like Hicks, Kevin White had a shin issue and then the first Bears pick of the 2015 draft never really did anything in his career. A back injury is never a good thing for a linebacker.
Has anyone heard anything on Elijah Hicks injury & possible return timeline? Reason I ask is he was a key contributor & big asset on Special Teams last season.
With people covering the team all but giving the practice squad journeyman a roster spot after one preseason effort, Davis came out of Week 2 in preseason with only one target and no catches. For Davis to make the roster as a fifth or sixth receiver, he'd need to be entirely useful as a return/coverage man. He had two kick returns of 29 and 19 yards and had punt returns of 12 and minus-1 yard. None of this speaks to kicking down the door and making a roster. Davis has to be so good that he causes the Bears to decide against keeping a player at another needed position. Game 2 was not that good.
I don't think anyone on the #Bears is a winner today,  but there are some losers. Kaden Davis- he just is a bad returner. Has good speed and shimmy with the ball in his hands,  but can't be relied to catch the ball. Logan Jones- two bad snaps just doesn't cut it for an older
His only preseason effort to date was 2-of-5 with a missed receiver near the goal line. His practice at Cincinnati turned up a nice completion to Dexter Lawrence, the Bengals defensive lineman. Johnson keeps getting asked about this and the answer is always the same. Status quo hasn't changed with the injured calf muscle. No one is sure.
At this point, it appears they're hoping Malik Muhammad can play there instead, but Muhammad struggled again in that position in Saturday's game. He's more of a boundary corner.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly of Bears Preseason Loss Includes Their Coach
full_text:
Even in being embarrassed by the Cincinnati Bengals for the second time in three days, the Bears had some good things happen.  The best thing was they got past another week of preseason.
Make no mistake, Saturday's 27-9 loss was the second defeat in three days .
The Bears might have tried to paint a smile face on their Thursday practice against the Bengals but when it ended the way it did, with the only really impressionable play of the day, then they can count it as a loss. That one play was with a real NFL defensive tackle, Dexter Lawrence, batting Caleb Williams' pass and then intercepting it himself.
Fortunately for the Bears, the only similar horrendous plays in Saturday's preseason game with the Bengals came from a collection of players who seem destined for the practice squad or worse. The bad news was these players were being used much earlier in the game than they should have been because injuries continue to be a problem.
Here is the good, the bad and the ugly from Bears preseason Game 2, including the postgame press conference for preseason Game 2.
Bears rookie sixth-round draft pick Jordan van den Berg takes flight. I put the clip in slow motion at the end. Enjoy. pic.twitter.com/eyQyukX6IS
Roschon Johnson resurrected his title as best Bears short-yardage back from the Matt Eberflus era. He powered for 2 yards on a run off right tackle behind the blocking of Jedrick Wills Jr. with 2:30 left before halftime on a fourth-and-1 at the Bears' own 15-yard line. Yes, the Bears were going for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 15. That's how starved for something positive they were, but at least they got it.
Then again, like with many of the positives they had in the game, this came after they had been stuffed like turkeys on third-and-1 running off the same side of the line. They had this third-down problem all game, whether it was the starters or subs on the field. They went 2-for-14, 1-for-7 in the first half. Going for first down from the shadow of your own goal posts in a preseason game doesn't really carry along with it the tag of success. It's more, well, they got it.
The Bears have found something in rookie Jordan van den Berg. The sixth-round pick out of Georgia Tech has been disruptive in the preseason. The South African is a freak athletically and you can see it translate to the field. Clocked a 1.61 10-yard split, 36” vert, 9’11” broad pic.twitter.com/3oParcxi11
The Bengals could only manage 3.2 yards per carry and for that the Bears' defensive front can thank more than Jordan van den Berg, although the rookie tackle definitely had an impact against the run on his 33 defensive plays. Or rather, he left an impact with his hitting in the Bengals.
"We were just trying to get out of our stance and strike blocks," Ben Johnson said. "I think our linebackers are doing a good job communicating and filling in the gaps. And then our little guys that are willing tacklers, I think they've done a good job tackling in space in two games for the most part."
The little guys haven't done a good job covering receivers in space, but that's for another category.
Give me 11 Jordan van den Bergs Bears rookie DT was everywhere last night. You can't teach this level of effort pic.twitter.com/pGUDljEzJZ
Not only did Braxton Jones get called for a holding penalty to wipe out a Roschon Johnson 10-yard run to the Bengals 7-yard line, but he also got bull-rushed backward on a play pass blocking after Caleb Williams had left. He had 15 total plays at left tackle, none of which stood out as works of football art.
And what of Jones' competition at left tackle? Theo Benedet emerged the clear winner but only because he didn't commit a penalty in the game. Jedrick Wills and Kiran Amegadjie had been competing at left tackle with Jones and were moved to right tackle. Both committed penalties, Wills a holding call and Amegadjie a false start.
It wasn't just Caleb Williams, as he only contributed five passes to the effort in the game. The Bears had a combined 72.8 passer rating for three QBs with a high of 75.4 by Case Keenum. It's usually not easy to be so bad at passing in preseason.
Caleb Williams is still wildly inaccurate. Still missing wide open receivers. Still has to have his hand held by the playcalls. If JJ McCarthy played like this in a pre-season game, the Twin Cities would look like the summer of 2020. pic.twitter.com/IhilFUpasr
The defense is all about rush and cover, says defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. The Bears did neither, except for one interception by safety Skyler Thomas and a QB hit each by Neville Gallimore, Dayo Odeyingbo, Jeremiah Martin and Nephi Sewell. And Sewell suffered what looked like a bad injury when he left on a cart. The Bears had no sacks, just those hits. And they gave up 282 passing yards, with a 103.2 paser rating on 25 of 38 to Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford.
Manning was part of the 103.2 passer rating but deserved his own special category for bad pass coverage with a TD throw allowed on the outside to both of the Bengals QBs.
DBs who get burned so badly in preseason by journeyman types don't get the tag of "toast." They simply wind up out of the league.
The Bengals are single-handedly sending Dontae Manning to the practice squad Dude is getting picked on damn near every snap pic.twitter.com/VNHsFbo32V
If you're looking for an explanation for the 103.2 passer rating allowed and a 7.4-yard average gain per pass play, look only at this list:
Kyler Gordon, Elijah Hicks, Coby Bryant, Tyrique Stevenson, Terell Smith, Jaylon Jones and William Wright. This was the long list of injured Bears DBs who didn't play. This includes three of their five starters in the secondary and two backups with experience. The Bears essentially used a practice squad secondary or less. Several of these injured players were expected back by now and had returned to practice on a limited basis, but weren't ready for a game.
One thing is certain. This preseason of injuries in the secondary has to end soon because preseason is ending soon. Nothing says the injuries will end, though.
Quite literally a hip drop tackle technique.. No call. Thankfully Colston Loveland wasn’t injured, but I was about to be really pissed. pic.twitter.com/MeCYggcPXg
After the game, Mr. Good, Better, Best was Mr. Bad, Worse, Worst at the press conference. Obviously unhappy about the performance, he deflected, was a bit obstinate and  dug up one of the oldest and ugliest postgame coaching phrases by saying he had to "look at the film" on more than one occasion.
His answer about why Williams was playing didn't produce much of an answer. He essentially said the QB didn't get enough reps during the week. But then he admitted Williams got nine more reps in the game. Nine more reps and five throws was worth putting the franchise QB on the field in a meaningless game, when they didn't even come against Lawrence and the Bengals' starting defense?  Williams could easily make up for those missed reps against the Titans this week, or even in practice.
Johnson also didn't handle a question about an overthrow Williams made well, saying his QB should have looked elsewhere to throw it when his pass sailed over Colston Loveland at the goal line.
This is the Caleb Williams miss to Colston Loveland down the middle. Ben Johnson said "I would probably go somewhere else with the ball on that one" during post game. Kaden Davis was an easy completion underneath. Colston was there but required some adjustment. #Bears pic.twitter.com/AyagsgJUzf
The goal of Johnson's play calling is to create separation. It succeeded here as Bengals DBs treated Loveland like he was contagious. If Williams had looked elsewhere, then someone should have been putting up All-22 film on social media to show how wide open Loveland was at the goal line without being targeted. Williams simply overthrew an open TD target, regardless of whether he was aiming at a proper receiver for the coverage on the play. And Johnson simply blew the…

title: Bears Have a Left Tackle Problem After Preseason Week 2 and Ozzy Trapilo is the Only Hope
full_text:
One of the most glaring issues from the Chicago Bears' preseason Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals was the struggles the team saw at left tackle .
Braxton Jones was the first man up at the position and played two series in total. He was then relieved by Theo Benedet, who played 22 snaps before ceding work to Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills.
Before his exit, Jones committed a holding penalty on the first series that helped wreck Chicago's drive, and he got straight up bullied on the second drive by a Bengals defender and nearly landed in the lap of Case Keenum.
Bear in mind, the Bengals weren't playing their starters on Saturday night.
Braxton Jones rep in the 2nd drive. Ozzy Trapilo needs to get back soon! pic.twitter.com/QfzzAdhXMd
In all, Jones finished with one pressure allowed, according to Pro Football Focus, and posted grades of 29.6 in pass-blocking and 54.4 in run-blocking. Not exactly encouraging work from the player who is considered the favorite at left tackle.
Benedet's raw PFF stats were better, with the veteran posting grades of 66.6 and 50.4 in run-blocking and pass protection, respectively, and he didn't give up a pressure.
But he also had back-to-back ugly reps before ultimately settling down a bit as the game progressed.
Tough back to back snaps for Theo here. (Typo saying Ozzy 1st time around) Oversets in the pass pro then overreaches the run after. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/5HCY7TvTLn
As for Amegadjie and Wills, the former gave up a team-high three pressures and notched PFF grades of 70.4 and 57.0 in the run and pass games, and Wills surrendered one pressure and had a solid 80.2 in pass pro but a dreadful 47.5 in run-blocking.
Add those showings to the lackluster performances Wills and Amegadjie had in preseason Week 1 and you can see why the Bears have a major concern at left and swing tackle.
When asked about the performances of the tackles after the game, head coach Ben Johnson didn't have any insight and instead noted that he has to watch the film first.
However, Johnson also expressed disappointment with the state of competitions throughout the roster during the week and he expressed his desire for more clarity while also pointing out Chicago's left tackle competition remains wide open.
Safe to say, the Bears won't have any more clarity after Saturday night.
What all this shows us is that the Bears badly need Ozzy Trapilo, who is projected to start once he's all the way back.
Trapilo looked to be the future at the position after a strong rookie season before his torn patellar and the lackluster performances of the aforementioned left tackle candidates have only boosted his stock further.
Trapilo was activated off the PUP list last week and is well ahead of schedule, but it remains to be seen if he'll be ready to go by Week 1. While Trapilo has been doing some work at practice , he has not taken part fully and it isn't clear when he'll be able to do so.
The concern with Trapilo is that he may not be himself in his first games or even year back, so his return doesn't mean Chicago is completely out of the woods.
In no world should the Bears rush Trapilo back, but the sooner he can get on the field, the better off the Bears will be because the guys who could fill in for him just aren't it as we enter the preseason's final week.
