title: 11 Winners, 5 Losers From Jaguars' Loss to Panthers: Josh Cameron Steps Up
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are almost through the preseason, with Friday night serving as a keen reminder of just how long we have to go until Week 1.
The Jaguars fell to the Carolina Panthers 34-17 during the second week of the preseason, and a number of the Jaguars' depth players made an impression ... whether positively or not.
So, who were the winners and losers of Friday's preseason bout with the Panthers? We break it all down below.
Liam Coen could have easily trotted the Jaguars starters out there, similar to what the Carolina Panthers did. But the risk/reward was never worth it, and as a result Coen and the Jaguars are entering next week without any new injuries to their 53-man roster candidates like they had the week before with Chuma Edoga. After a productive joint practice earlier in the week, Coen deserves credit for making the right call with the Jaguars' starting lineup by sitting them.
"I definitely liked what I saw from the joint practice," Coen said following Friday's game. "I was pleased with the physicality, the effort, the energy and a lot of the execution. There is a ton to continue to clean up here obviously. (The Joint Practice) was a step in the right direction as you look at – not necessarily milestones in Training Camp, but good moments (we) can draw on and say, ‘hey, that’s our brand of football’ on display against another quality opponent."
Both Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs played a decent bit on Friday, which is the same way the Jaguars approached it with the duo a week ago in New Orleans. Each had some flashes, such as Combs recording a quarterback hit to force a third-down incompletion and Miller making some physical plays against the run. But the real reason they are both winners is because of what Coen said after the game.
"I think at some point here, we're all going to understand they're both going to play. Like, they're both very different players. They both have different skill sets," Coen said.
"Whoever ends up being number one on the depth chart is obviously semantics in a lot of ways. I was pleased with Ventrell. I've been pleased with him for over the last few days. I thought he had a good Joint as well, but we're going to need both of them. We're going to need both of those guys to play significant snaps for us within their roles and within how the game on defense needs to be called and the offenses we're seeing, the situations that we're in. We're going to need them both. So, whoever ends up as number one, it's going to end up being a lot of reps for them both.
In short ... it does not matter who "starts". They have both earned some snaps in the Jaguars' defense moving forward, and Coen made that clear on Friday night.
Nick Mullens responded well this week after a tough outing against the New Orleans Saints. He was a bit injured at the start of the week but came back and had some of the best practices he has had all summer, and he then played well against the Panthers on Friday. Mullens was 6-of-7 for 65 yards, and would have been 7-for-7 with a touchdown pass as well had Ameer Abdullah not dropped a touchdown early in the contest in the red-zone. QB2 is here to stay.
"I thought he did some good things. They had not all their starters in but they did have some and I thought he was on time, in rhythm, getting the ball out," Coen said. "We catch the ‘choice’ (route) down at the goal line. We were going to be 7-7 at that point, right? And, you know, I thought Nick did a nice job. I thought they protected well when Nick was in as well early on and kind of got a little tired later on but for the most part I thought we protected fairly well as well."
No player did more for their case to be on the 53-man roster on Friday than veteran running back Ameer Abdullah. He was the Jaguars' offense against the Panthers, getting the starting nod after not suiting up a week ago against the Saints. With LeQuint Allen out for at least the rest of training camp, Abdullah is the one who is stepping up on the depth chart. Abdullah looked electric on Friday and could become a piece of the roster few saw coming when camp kicked off. If he can pass-protect, he will be in a good spot moving forward.
ANKLES Ameer Abdullah goes for 23! #CARvsJAX on CBS47 pic.twitter.com/aJsTiDA5Bx
The Jaguars' rookie receivers might be needed earlier than expected if Jakobi Meyers misses any time with a hand injury. The good news is that the Jaguars gave both Josh Cameron and CJ Williams the chance to make plays on Saturday, and each stepped up. The Jaguars completed all six targets to the sixth-round duo, and Cameron made one of the best plays of the entire night on a deep shot from Nick Mullens. These two just keep impressing.
"My boy @Josh_Cameron34 ballin'!" @TravisHunterJr on kicking FGs and more. #CARvsJAX on CBS47 pic.twitter.com/PUGiMIBCUx
"The guys (Josh and CJ) are such pros. They have a lot to learn, no question. But in terms of showing up early, leaving late, doing extra, being locked into the details, and understanding how to walk thru in some of the walk thru settings. And then they come out into the lights, and they make plays," Coen said Friday. "It’s good to see Josh make a one-on-one op that we’ve seen in practice a number of times. Nick gave him a good opportunity. CJ continuing to be steady. Those guys are earning trust for sure and they’re going to continue to earn more."
Joey Aguilar didn't get much run in the first preseason game, but that changed on Friday when he was given several drives at the helm of the Jaguars' offense. He led the Jaguars to two scoring drives late and went 9-of-10 for 130 yards, showing off a willingness to test defenses deep and the ability to actually come through on the promise. He has a big arm and prototype size, and he certainly looked the part on Friday. It was his most impressive day as a Jaguar yet, and it will be interesting to see if he can now push for the QB3 job.
The Jaguars found two undrafted gems at defensive end a year ago with Danny Striggow and B.J. Green, and there could be another one in 2026 with Bryan Thomas Jr. The South Carolina product has flashed all camp, had a good game last week against the Saints, and then came back on Friday and had another impressive outing. He is getting some consistent pressure, but he is also flashing against the run.
Trebor Peña led the Jaguars in receiving for the second week in a row, and he certainly seems like he is making a strong case for the practice squad. The undrafted wide receiver caught four passes for 72 yards and a touchdown, and the Jaguars are quickly finding out that he has a solid back-and-forth with Aguilar when the lights come on.
"Yeah, proud of Pena, again, just continues to make plays being in the right spot at the right time. I think him and Joey have a natural little connection from working together, obviously, in a lot of these settings and practice," Coen said.
Another undrafted wide receiver who showed up was Michael Wortham, who caught three passes for 41 yards. Wortham has stood out at camp in recent days and the speedy slot receiver had a few standout reps against the Panthers, including some impressive yards after the catch on a wide receiver screen. He is another young receiver who looks like a natural candidate for the practice squad.
"I thought Michael Wortham did some nice things as well tonight. He's kind of been flashing a little bit. Got a lot of reps in the joint the other day as well and didn't flinch, didn't blink," Coen said.
The Jaguars' pair of rookie tight ends didn't do anything disappointing in any form on Friday, but the lack of action for either was a bit disappointing since it seems like they simply need reps. Nate Boerkircher did not play, resting with the Jaguars' starters and other key players, so we are now through two preseason games without a target for the No. 56 pick. title: Good, Not So Good From Jaguars' Preseason Loss to Panthers: Ameer Abdullah Shines
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Another preseason game is in the books, and that means another chance for us to look at The Good and The Not So Good.
So, what were the highs and the lows of the Jaguars' preseason loss to the Carolina Panthers? We break it all down below.
Sometimes, the easy choice is the right one. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicated early in the week that the Jaguars starters might play a bit against the Panthers, but he seemed to reverse course after joint practice on Wednesday and then officially kept the starters off the field once kickoff came around on Friday night.
Considering some of the senseless injuries that happen in the preseason, this is the only decision Coen could really make. Not all teams are wise enough to keep their starters out of pointless games for the sake of reps that, ultimately, do not count, but Coen and the Jaguars made the right call with their squad
Outside of one of Ventrell Miller/Branson Combs, the Jaguars' first defense on Friday night did not have a single starter on it. Add in the fact that they were going against the Panthers' starting offense from Wednesday's joint practices, including quarterback Bryce Young and star wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan, and the Jaguars' defense had a big test to start the game. While they did eventually give up a touchdown to the Panthers on the second drive of the game, the first drive was extremely encouraging from the Jaguars' group of backups.
After Combs was able to register a quarterback hit on the first third-down the Jaguars saw, Jacksonville was able to get the Panthers off the field after just four plays and nine yards. Combs was hit for a defensive pass interference at the start of the drive after he was matched up with McMillan, but he got a pressure against the Panthers' best on third-down and the Jaguars' backup defense got an early win against the Panthers' top unit.
As far as preseason wins go, that is a significant one. The Jaguars' defense let Carolina have some big plays during joint practices earlier in the week, but they came out to play on Friday night.
If there is any player who really popped on Friday, it was veteran running back Ameer Abdullah. We have said all training camp that Abdullah has consistently made plays and has established himself as the Jaguars' RB4, and he got a big chance to show what he can do with extended run on Friday. He played the first half, recording six carries for 45 yards and three catches for 37 yards, making him one of the game's most productive players.
With the Jaguars dealing with a LeQuint Allen injury for at least the rest of training camp, Abdullah makes the most sense to get a bump up on the depth chart. With performances like the one on Friday, where he had a 23-yard carry and a nice 18-yard catch-and-run in the passing game, Abdullah could be playing himself onto the 53-man roster depending on the status of Allen come Week 1.
DeeJay Dallas was already fighting an uphill climb when it came to the Jaguars' roster configuration, and it is tough to say that Friday night helped his case. Abdullah has already leaped him on the depth chart and then played well against the Panthers, undrafted rookie running back J'Mari Taylor has flashed at times, and it could be hard to see Dallas with a role even on the practice squad as a result.
When a player is facing those kind of odds entering the middle of the preseason, they can't afford to make many mistakes. That is exactly what Dallas did on the first drive of the second half however, fumbling a handoff that the Panthers recovered to end a Jaguars drive early. Dallas does not have much margin for error, and this was a tough blunder to overlook.
Friday night was a rough outing for backup quarterback Carter Bradley. The context is required of course that he was playing behind the Jaguars' third-team offensive line, but Bradley's final numbers read as follows: 6-of-13 passing (46.2% completion) for 51 yards and an interception. This gave him just 3.9 yards per attempt compared to 9.3 from Nick Mullens earlier in the night.
Bradley has some interesting traits as a developmental quartrback, but I got the sense from the fan base last week that they wanted to see him push Mullens as the QB2. I never thought this would actually happen, and Friday night was another example of why. Mullens, even for his own faults, is simply on a different level right now than Bradley, who still has to pove he is a better option than Joey Aguilar for the practice squad quarterback spot.
Friday just felt flat for the Jaguars. That is going to happen when you sit the best players on the team for the entirety of the game, but even the Jaguars' backups failed to make the kind of plays that the Panthers' backups made. The Jaguars did not record a single pass-breakup despite the Panthers dropping back more than 35 times, and the lack of turnovers that seemed to irk Liam Coen carried over to Friday.
Just because the Jaguars' starters didn't play doesn't mean the field was completely lacking conttributors. But a secondary that had Caleb Ransaw, Jalen Huskey, Jabbar Muhammad, and Christian Braswell playing for long stretches was not able to make a play all game, which is a bit concerning when it comes to the Jaguars' depth.

title: 5 Observations on the Jaguars' Preseason Loss to Panthers: Liam Coen Makes Right Call
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The preseason is alive and strong in Duval.
The Jaguars wrapped up Week 2 of the preseason against the Carolina Panthers at EverBank Stadium on Friday night ___
So, what did we see from the Jaguars and their backups against the Panthers, and what does it mean moving forward? We break it all down below, live from the action in Jacksonville.
Outside of whichever linebacker starts between Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs, the Jaguars did not have a single starter dress for Friday's game against the Panthers. Things seemed to trend in that direction as the week went on, and it eventually became clear that this was the only direction the Jaguars could really go in. That means the real test for the starters will come one way or another next week against the Carolina Panthers.
Whether the Jaguars would any players of significant 16 days before Week 1 once the preseason finale is here next Friday remains to be seen, but the Jaguars will have two joint practices with the Buccaneers before then. That should give the Jaguars all of the time they need to put together what they want to
Third downs were already interesting for  the Jaguars' defense last season, with defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile throwing everything and the kitchen sink at opposing offenses. The way Campanile deployed passing-down looks was a direct factor to the Jaguars' massive improvement in terms of turnovers, and it appears he is looking to do more of the same when the Jaguars' defense takes the field in 2026.
On the first obvious passing down of the game, the Jaguars deployed the package that I expect will be their most popular passing-down package this season: a dime look with four defensive linemen, one linebacker, and six defensive backs. The Jaguars have experimented a ton with this kind of package in camp, using it to get four cornerbacks on the field together or to get three safeties alongside three cornerbacks.
The Jaguars got good results from their first look of it on Friday, too. Combs was the lone linebacker on the field, and he was sent by Campanile as a blitzer. He beat the running back and recorded a quarterback hit on Bryce Young to force the incompletion and a punt in the process.
Jonathon Brooks isn't going to see the field on 3rd down much if he can't pass protect pic.twitter.com/cNuQfEic7v
The first-team offense the Jaguars rolled out on Friday night had very few players who will get snaps by the time the regular-season rolls around, which meant eyes were always going to be fixed on rookie receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron. The sixth-round picks did not disappoint, either, with each following up their strong performances from Wednesday's joint practices with even stronger ones against the Panthers on Friday.
Cameron and Williams each played for most of the first half, and they proved to be the favorite targets for the Jaguars' backup duo of Nick Mullens and Carter Bradley. Cameron caught both of his two targets for 41 yards, including a stellar rep on a downfield route on a 22-yard gain in the first quarter where he was able to stack the cornerback and then pluck the ball out of the air.
Williams stood out a good bit as well, catching all four of his targets for 22 yards. He did not generate an explosive play like Cameron did, but he was used as a reliable possession receiver who kept the offense on schedule, and he was able to do exactly that. It was a good night for the young guys.
The Jaguars' starting offensive line on Friday night as was follows: Kilian Zierer, Ricky Lee, Sam Mustipher, Sam Carvin, and Jimto Obidegwu. None of these players are expected to be on the Jaguars' 53-man roster in a few weeks, and the Jaguars essentially rolled out their complete third-team unit instead of playing any starters or even second-teamers.
Considering the injuries the Jaguars have faced at the offensive line position over the last few weeks, this seems like the only call the Jaguars could have made. They were never going to play clear starters like Anton Harrison, Ezra Cleveland, or Robert Hainsey, but it also would not have made much sense for the Jaguars to risk an injury to Emmanuel Pregnon or Jonah Monheim.
Add in Chuma Edoga and Wyatt Milum being banged up and Daniel Faalele just getting here a few days ago, and this was quite the makeshift offensive line. I would expect we get a closer look at what a Week 1 starting offensive line might look like in joint practices with the Buccaneers next week.
If there is one player who seems like he did a lot for his stock on Friday night, it was veteran backup running back Ameer Abdullah. The 12th-year pro has clearly taken the role of RB4 throughout the course of camp and has been over the likes of J'Mari Taylor and DeeJay Dallas on the depth chart, and he could have the chance to actually see the field at the start of the year considering the injury that the Jaguars are now dealing with when it comes to LeQuint Allen.
If Friday's showing was any indication, Abdullah still has something left in the tank to give. It wasn't all perfect since he did drop a touchdown pass in the red-zone early in the game, but he had an explosive 23-yard run that showed speed and the ability to force missed tackles in the open field. He also had an 18-yard catch-and-run that displayed the value he can still bring the Jaguars in the passing game.
Abdullah's exact role and importance will have to rely on the status of Allen, but it is more than fair to say that he has done enough to at least earn the consideration in Allen's time off the field.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers From Chiefs' Preseason Week 2 Loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
full_text:
The Chiefs dropped their eighth straight preseason game Saturday night in Tampa Bay, which of course means absolutely nothing. They did not capture a win in either of the previous two preseason years. One of those years they went to the Super Bowl. The other, they went 6-11. Take the record for what it is worth.
What does matter is what the individual performances told us, and there was plenty to digest.
Before getting into the biggest winners and losers, it is worth noting that safety Jaden Hicks, defensive tackle Marcus Harris, and running back Emmett Johnson all played well enough to be in the winners column.
Harrison Butker was a mixed bag, drilling an incredible 69-yarder and starting the preseason going 7-for-7, which also included two 59-yard field goals, before missing two kicks. One would have made the score a 16-16 game by the end of it, and the other a 43-yard kick with just over three minutes to go, missing a likely game-winner.
Let’s dive into the three biggest winners and losers of this 16-15 loss to the Bucs.
As a fifth-round pick from just a year ago, wide receiver Jalen Royals may have solidified his place on this team Saturday night. That is not usually a concern for second-year draftees, but Royals had shown very little up until this point.
That changed in Tampa Bay.
He was targeted six times and hauled in all six, showcasing the yards-after-the-catch ability that made him an attractive pick out of Utah State. His six catches between Justin Fields and Garrett Nussmeier netted 51 yards, and he was the Chiefs' highest-graded receiver on the night, according to PFF.
For a player whose roster spot has been quietly in question, Saturday was a statement.
Saturday night may have been the best we have seen from defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in a Chiefs uniform. In 16 pass -rush snaps, the four-year veteran supplied four pressures and delivered the biggest highlight of the night, flattening Buccaneers backup quarterback Jake Browning for his first sack of the preseason.
His 26.7 pass-rush win rate led all Chiefs defensive linemen. For a former first-round pick whose career has been defined by injuries and unfulfilled potential, this was the kind of performance that could propel the former Kansas State Wildcat into the starting lineup.
Defensive end R Mason Thomas did not light up the box score, but this is in recognition of his continued showing from a week ago. In 10 true pass sets, the rookie again supplied pressure, collecting a hurry and a quarterback hit.
For an undersized pass rush specialist at 6-foot-2 and 249 pounds, that kind of consistency is exactly what the Chiefs were hoping to see, especially on third downs. Having someone who can generate quick pressure and allow Chris Jones and George Karlaftis to clean up is something this team has been missing for years.
Both Thomas and Anudike-Uzomah stepping up simultaneously is a particularly welcome sight given that Ashton Gillotte's injury timetable remains uncertain. With both stepping up last night, Chiefs OnSI’s Jordan Foote noted that Gillotte’s absence may not be the doomsday scenario we all thought.
Right tackle Kahlil Benson drew the start at right tackle, which is something he had been building toward all training camp. How the depth chart looks when the Chiefs return to practice Monday will be worth monitoring, because Saturday was not a good showing.
He essentially whiffed on two pass sets, with one resulting in a strip sack and the other forcing an incomplete pass, with Justin Fields needing to get rid of the ball quicker than anticipated. He graded out as the worst pass blocker on the field according to PFF with a 33.4, allowing two pressures in 11 true pass sets.
The one silver lining, if you can call it that: Jaylon Moore graded out second-worst on the team with a PFF pass blocking grade of 40.7, so neither tackle distinguished himself Saturday night.
It is somewhat unclear how realistic it is for cornerback Melvin Smith to make the 53-man roster when cutdown day arrives a week from now. He seems like a prime candidate to slip through waivers and onto the practice squad.
That said, he was treated as more of a contributor than veteran Kristian Fulton last week, which made Saturday's performance more consequential. He graded out worse than any other defensive back, allowing four catches for 38 yards on four targets.
The names doing the damage, Ko Kieft, Kameron Johnson, Dean Patterson, and Eric Rivers, are not exactly household names. That is an uneasy sign when the opening regular season assignment would be Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton. A four-phase special teamer was his likely role anyway, but he did not look remotely ready for a defensive role.
Tight end Jared Wiley was technically third on the team with two catches and 15 receiving yards, but he was targeted four times and had a drop. He looks smooth catching passes in open space, but Travis Kelce and Noah Gray already fill that role.
What the Chiefs need from a third tight end is someone willing to do the dirty work, and Wiley has not shown that.
For the second straight week, second-year undrafted free agent Jake Briningstool collected three catches for 28 or more yards and has shown solid open-field blocking as well. Briningstool is not a road grader either, but he is contributing more to the offense.
Wiley's roster spot will depend heavily on how the Chiefs construct the rest of the 53. If they keep four running backs or push toward seven wide receivers, given how Royals, Nikko Remigio, and Andrew Armstrong have shown specific skill sets, four tight ends may be off the table.

title: Too Good to Hide: Garrett Nussmeier's Promising Preseason Could Force the Chiefs' Hand
full_text:
Take a look around the NFL at any given moment, and you'll quickly be confronted with a universal truth: there just aren't enough good quarterbacks.
A large swath of the league permanently resides in quarterback purgatory, while even the lucky few teams with franchise signal-callers have to find capable backups for when injuries inevitably arrive.
At age 41, Joe Flacco is on a one-year, $6 million deal to back up Joe Burrow in Cincinnati. The Los Angeles Rams, with reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, spent a first-round pick on Ty Simpson in hopes of avoiding the QB carousel in a post-Stafford world. The Cleveland Browns have sunk remarkable draft capital and absurd amounts of cash into their current quarterback room, resulting in nothing but disasters at every turn.
You may already understand what this has to do with rookie Chiefs quarterback Garrett Nussmeier.
Through two preseason games, Nussmeier has looked like an NFL quarterback. Not a Week 1 starter—not even like a player who is about to jump current backup Justin Fields on KC's depth chart—but like a quarterback who has a place on a professional football field, with potential to grow from there.
When the Chiefs selected Nussmeier in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, his spot on the 53-man roster was far from guaranteed. He was the ninth-to-last pick of the draft (No. 249 of 257), but it was a noteworthy swing at the time.
With Patrick Mahomes as the team's superstar and Fields as the clear backup for 2026, Nussmeier may have chosen to go elsewhere if he would have been an undrafted free agent. Instead, the Chiefs used their last pick to ensure that he'd join their quarterback room, at least for offseason activities, training camp, and the preseason.
A draft pick spent on a quarterback is always a cause for some intrigue, but Nussmeier's pedigree made Kansas City's selection even more alluring.
In an October 2024 mock draft that projected how the 2025 NFL Draft would play out, Chris Trapasso of CBS Sports mocked Nussmeier at No. 12 overall .
"Right this very instant, if there's one quarterback I had to choose to ascend boards over the next four months, it'd be Nussmeier, who plays with such effortless arm talent, accuracy, and toughness within the pocket," Trapasso wrote nearly two years ago.
Instead of leaving as a potential first-round pick after the 2024 season, Nussmeier stayed at LSU , ultimately hurting his draft stock as he battled through injuries in a disappointing year for the Tigers.
Still, Nussmeier earned a third-round grade in the KCSN Draft Guide , which slotted him in as the No. 3 quarterback in the class. When the Chiefs took Nussmeier in the seventh round, he was the 10th quarterback to be selected.
Again, none of that guaranteed anything for Nussmeier, but it's important context to remember when trying to project what his career could become.
In two preseason games, Nussmeier has seemed comfortable running the Chiefs' offense , looking less like a seventh-round pick and more like a player with more than 1,000 pass attempts at an SEC powerhouse.
This has all come in a very small sample size, and it's far from an assurance that he'll become the long-term answer as Mahomes' multi-year backup, but it's also how the rest of the league will be looking at Nussmeier if the Chiefs decide that they don't have room for three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster .
Nussmeier has made the cut in our Chiefs On SI roster projections, but the Chiefs have preferred to carry only two quarterbacks in recent years, allowing that extra roster spot to go to another position group.
Personally, I've seen enough from Nussmeier to make the call. He's worth protecting on the 53-man roster this season, with hopes that his development in Kansas City could lead him to a career that far exceeds his seventh-round draft selection.
If the Chiefs don't agree, there are plenty of quarterback-poor teams that would be wise to give him a longer look.

title: Chiefs Snap Count Analysis: Reading Between the Lines After Game vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
All 32 NFL teams are still learning about their respective rosters at this stage, and the Kansas City Chiefs are no different. The club's second preseason outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers featured plenty of tweaks from the week prior, which showed up primarily in how snaps were divvied up.
In the opener against the Los Angeles Rams, it was the first taste of somewhat real football since Kansas City's season ended in early January. With that came overreactions galore, but this most recent bout at Raymond James Stadium brought a few of those questions into clearer focus. The division of labor from Andy Reid and his staff might've tipped how the coaches feel about a select handful of players.
Now that snap counts have been released, what jumped off the page? Let's take a look at three noteworthy takeaways from another week of Chiefs football.
With Xavier Worthy and Rashee Rice attempting to ensure that they're 100% healthy for Week 1 of the regular season, the Chiefs have given supporting pieces of the wide receiver room opportunities to showcase their talents this preseason. Prospects Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen, Day 3 NFL Draft pickups from the 2025 and 2026 NFL Drafts , naturally draw the most attention of those remaining on the list.
Allen's star didn't shine nearly as bright in his second unofficial game as a pro, but Royals made the most of yet another heavy workload.
For the second weekend in a row, the former fourth-round selection played a whopping 36 snaps on offense. Sure, that can oftentimes be a reflection of someone who isn't part of a team's plans, but Royals' context makes it feel like a different scenario. He needs the reps to flash any sort of improvement in his sophomore year, which he did on Saturday. Playing with multiple quarterbacks, he led the Kansas City offense in targets and receptions (six), as well as yards with 51.
In a downright critical year for Royals' development, he was a slow burner at camp but made more plays over time. That trend has been replicated in preseason play.
The Chiefs knew coming into the preseason that first-round rookie Mansoor Delane would step into a starting role on the boundary as long as his shoulder injury healed up in time . That wound up being the case, with the No. 6 overall pick playing on Saturday and earning 11 snaps alongside projected starter Nohl Williams . The real uncertainty revolved around the slot position, especially with  each contender for the job coming with some baggage.
Free agent signing Kader Kohou is coming off a torn ACL and didn't play against LA due to injury. L'Jarius Sneed hasn't been active at all this preseason. Jadon Canady, for all the promise he brings, is a Day 3 rookie . Chris Roland Wallace is more of a safety-nickel hybrid than a true every-down player. Did defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo accidentally tip his hand with how he utilized Kohou down in Tampa?
The former Miami Dolphins standout had one special teams snap on kickoff coverage and played only seven reps on defense, in the same ballpark as high-profile starters. Each of those snaps saw him line up in the slot, via Pro Football Focus . This could've been merely an instance of load management and Spagnuolo wanting to get Kohou's feet wet a bit, although it also could've been an unwritten message that the 27-year-old is still slated to fill the void most expected when he signed.
Yes, I'm cheating here and weaving two positions into one takeaway. Rules, even self-imposed ones, are meant to be broken.
A week ago, Emari Demercado's usage seemed to throw a fork in the blueprint those in Chiefs circles anticipated for the running back room. He didn't play until the second half versus the Rams and was also utilized equally as much on special teams as on offense.
The Buccaneers game depicted someone who will get work during the regular season, however, as the offseason acquisition had 21 offensive snaps. Rookie Emmett Johnson (25) and 2025 seventh-rounder Brashard Smith (14) also saw the field plenty, but it's now increasingly evident that Demercado doesn't appear to be on the outside looking in.
At the tackle position, both Jaylon Moore and Kahlil Benson looked bad against the Tampa Bay pass rush. Benson stayed in the game far longer than his elder counterpart, though, playing 35 snaps to Moore's 12. The latter mark aligned with the first-team protectors, signaling Moore being the clear leader for the right tackle job once Josh Simmons returns healthy on the left.
Benson's story remains awesome, and he likely isn't going anywhere once it's time for roster cutdowns, but a healthy version of the Chiefs' offensive line figures to have Moore in it and not him.

title: Andy Reid Won’t Ignore Chiefs’ Preseason Struggles After Another Blown Lead
full_text:
Had yesterday's preseason loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers been a regular season game, it would have been one of the more heartbreaking defeats the Chiefs have suffered in recent years. They snatched defeat from the jaws of victory in the second half, largely due to an erratic performance from veteran kicker Harrison Butker .
Most NFL fans agree that winning preseason games doesn't determine how teams perform when the actual season comes around. However, fans might be surprised to learn that the Chiefs now haven't won a preseason game in 1,093 days.
The last time K.C. came out on top in an exhibition was in August 2023, when they defeated the Cleveland Browns 33-32 in a thriller at Arrowhead Stadium. Since then, the Chiefs have appeared in two Super Bowls and won one, but haven't been on the winning end of a preseason matchup. To some, this is a quirky stat that means nothing in the long run. But to Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, there is a tiny level of concern knowing that the team hasn't been able to get it done in eight consecutive tries, even if it's mostly the second and third teams getting the majority of the reps.
"Listen, it's America. You want to win everything you do," Reid said about preseason games. "That's how it goes. So, to say you don't want to win, these guys want to do that. We just got to eliminate some of these mistakes, but again, you're doing that and trying to evaluate everybody at the same time."
There is a level of attention to detail that NFL players must have, regardless of whether they're playing with the starters or backups. Reid's frustration is not surprising given the unusual string of losses K.C. has suffered in the preseason.
In each of Kansas City's two preseason games this year, the Chiefs led going into the fourth quarter yet were unable to hold off the opposing team's offense. Everyone will probably forget about this stat going into the Week 1 opener against the Broncos, and there's still an opportunity for them to break the streak next Saturday against the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks.
One thing is for certain is that the Chiefs' coaches will be ripping their players a new one following yesterday's effort that caused them to blow the lead.

title: Despite Rough Output, Chiefs' QBs Supported for Performance vs. Buccaneers
full_text:
Sometimes, it simply isn't your day. That was made clear at multiple spots for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, as everything ranging from scoring points to executing situational football or avoiding getting in their own way seemed to be an uphill battle all night long.
There were some bright spots, namely wide receiver Jalen Royals on the offensive side of the ball and safeties Jaden Hicks and DeShon Singleton on defense. Despite what the box score says, head coach Andy Reid believes his quarterback trio also belongs in that group.
The collective of Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun posted a combined stat line of completing 23 of 35 passes for just 155 yards, no touchdowns and in interception. It was an ugly showing by about every measurement available, yet Reid still gleans something positive.
Taking the podium shortly after the conclusion of Saturday's Chiefs preseason game , Reid kicked his quarterback-related thoughts off by complimenting his rookie for making some tough throws.
"I'll go back and look at it a little closer, but if you're asking specifically about Nuss, I thought he had some nice throws in there," Reid said. "There were a couple where they were tight throws — I've got to look at the route to see if we should've maybe been a little more aggressive coming back to the ball in those tight situations, but it looked like he handled things well. He's getting more comfortable."
He then continued by addressing Fields making the most of his mobility and shielding Oladokun from some of the blame regarding his late-game turnover.
"Justin, I thought, had some good plays in there," Reid said. "A couple of nice throws on the move. And then Chris, you know, Chris had a big third-down play that got tipped and dropped and intercepted. That really gave them a big advantage. Listen, those things happen. You've got to go through them, learn from them and move forward."
Based on sheer efficiency, Fields was the most productive Kansas City signal-caller on Saturday. He completed nine of his 12 passes for 64 yards, also carrying the ball once for a 15-yard gain on third-and-10. Oladokun, whose pass to tight end Tre Watson was imperfect but entirely catchable, had that go down as his lone incompletion but averaged all of 2.8 yards per pass.
Nussmeier was somewhere in the middle, both statistically and via the eye test. In all, he completed just over half of his 17 throws and mustered 74 yards on them. He offered both pluses and minuses with his play once again, whether it be climbing in the pocket to deliver a 17-yard strike to wideout Jalen Royals or making back-to-back passes that were poorly timed and could've been picked off by a better defensive back.
As is frequently the case in the preseason, some of the raw numbers were out of the quarterback's control or didn't show up in a traditional sense. For example, TruMedia reveals that Fields' aforementioned run brought the second-most EPA (expected points added) on offense at 2.5. Nussmeier's deep-ball heave to receiver Andrew Armstrong, which ended in a defensive pass interference call, took the cake at 3.2.
On the flip side, Oladokun's partial-fault interception slotted into the other end of the spectrum (-4.6). Fields also had some lackluster pocket navigation this weekend, worsened by poor tackle play. A 20-yard sack in the first half immediately comes to mind as an example of teach tape in both realms.
Ups and downs are a natural part of the quarterback position, which Reid has always been consistent about. As the Chiefs work to figure out how many field generals they'll carry on the eventual 53-man roster, the legendary head coach is going beyond the data on this one.

title: Andy Reid Backs Harrison Butker After Chiefs Kicker’s Up-And-Down Showing
full_text:
Longtime Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker was on his way to becoming the hero against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tonight — until he was the exact opposite.
The three-time Super Bowl winner accounted for all nine of Kansas City's points in the first half, connecting on field goals from 45 and 58 yards before drilling an incredible 69-yarder as time expired. Although the NFL doesn't count preseason statistics toward the record books, this would have been the NFL's longest-made field goal had it been tracked. The kick sailed through the uprights with several yards of room to spare, giving K.C. a two-possession lead heading into halftime.
But Butker's strong night took a turn after the break, missing an important extra point following Emmett Johnson's touchdown run before pushing a 43-yard field goal wide right with just over three minutes remaining. The attempt came from the right hash and never hooked back toward the middle. Had he made it, the kick would have put the Chiefs up by two and potentially won them their first preseason game since August 2023.
Ironically, Butker's two misses came on his shortest attempts of the night, emphasizing the inconsistency that has crept into his game . Still, head coach Andy Reid made it clear after the contest that he has the utmost confidence in his kicker.
"I trust him. That happens," Reid said. "He'll learn from it and move on. He's made enough of the big ones for us. He's just got to make it. He'll make an adjustment there."
Reid has plenty of reason to feel that way, as Butker has delivered countless big kicks for the Chiefs. He sent them to the Super Bowl in 2023 with a game-winning field goal against the Bengals and forced overtimes in the 2022 divisional round against the Bills and the 2024 Super Bowl against the 49ers. His list of clutch moments in the red and gold goes on and on. Butker is one of the league's more reliable legs, finishing 33-of-38 on field goals last season. However, that was the third-lowest conversion rate of his career, and he also missed four extra points and posted the worst PAT% of his career.
The leg strength is obviously still there for Butker to remain among the NFL's elite kickers, even if his accuracy has dipped somewhat from his peak. At 31 years old, he has plenty of his prime ahead of him, and Reid and the Chiefs clearly haven't lost faith in him despite tonight's up-and-down showing.

title: Andy Reid Drops Mixed Bag of Injury News on Alohi Gilman, Tyreke Smith After Chiefs' Loss
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs had more things go their way in Saturday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers than the week before, yet it still ended in the same result of a loss. Additionally, the visitors were hit with a pair of injuries by the time the dust settled on the club's second preseason game of 2026.
Two players, safety Alohi Gilman and defensive end Tyreke Smith, were ruled out by Kansas City on Saturday via social media. Gilman's designation came concurrently with the start of action at Raymond James Stadium, which saw him fail to play a single snap alongside the rest of the starters. Smith's ailment popped up in the second half of play, resulting in him not returning.
What's the latest scoop? Speaking to the media following Saturday's 16-15 shortcoming in Tampa, head coach Andy Reid provided an update. It appears to be nothing major for Gilman, but there's more evaluating that needs to be done on the Smith front.
"As far as the injuries go, Alohi, in warmups, had some low-back spasms," Reid said. "So he didn't play, and then Tyreke Smith tweaked his right hamstring. I'm not sure how bad that is, but it was bad enough where he couldn't continue on there."
No injury can ever be determined a positive, but it is a silver lining for the Chiefs that Gilman avoided anything serious. The offseason free agent pickup is expected to be a playmaker in coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's defensive backfield, and he's endeared himself to fellow teammates by stepping up as a leader . Losing him for any portion of the regular season would've bordered on catastrophic depending on the timeline.
The bad news for Smith is he desperately needed a strong performance and some luck to potentially make the final 53-man roster ahead of the regular season. Given that George Karlaftis, Ashton Gillotte , Felix Anudike-Uzomah, R Mason Thomas and newcomer Emmanuel Ogbah were all viewed as above him on the depth chart at a minimum, getting banged up is undoubtedly a tough break.
The 26-year-old played 19 defensive snaps and another six on special teams a week ago against the Los Angeles Rams, recording a tackle on the opening kickoff but failing to register another box score statistic the rest of the way. In his work versus the Buccaneers, he had a lone solo tackle.
An already less-than-100% Chiefs team continued to get some bad luck on the health front this weekend, although the majority of its starters remain unscathed with one preseason contest remaining.

title: Four Takeaways From the Chiefs' 16-15 Loss to the Buccaneers
full_text:
Coming off a one-score loss to the Los Angeles Rams last Saturday, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the road looking to secure their first preseason win since 2023. Unfortunately for them, that elusive victory couldn't be captured against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
In a game Kansas City initially led, special teams mistakes and some late-game stalling on both sides led to a narrow 16-15 defeat at Raymond James Stadium. The Chiefs now drop to 0-2 this August, but the outing left plenty to digest with next Friday's finale versus the Seattle Seahawks on the horizon.
With that in mind, here are four takeaways from Saturday's game.
The Chiefs got a bad break this week when head coach Andy Reid revealed that defensive end Ashton Gillotte suffered a ruptured plantar fascia . The foot injury is will hold the second-year pass rusher out for the remainder of the preseason, also potentially putting his Week 1 availability in question. Even if he's deemed healthy enough to play early in the regular season, should it render him less effective than normal, KC may need to pivot quickly.
In that event, the club is getting a long look at some potential replacements given that Gilotte missed the preseason opener as well. Felix Anudike-Uzomah, entering a contract year , is finally healthy and delivered a thunderous sack in the first half. Second-round pick R Mason Thomas continues to flash his patented burst and athleticism up front. Losing Gillotte's floor as a run defender would hurt, but perhaps things aren't quite as bad off as they seem.
The early returns on the Emmanuel Ogbah signing are a different story.
The past few years have been tough for Harrison Butker, who was once a consensus pick for being one of the best kickers in the sport. After an injury-shortened 2022, he was excellent in 2023 but made only 85.7% of his field goals and the same share of his extra points over the course of the ensuing two seasons. He admitted this offseason that he's looking to put this past campaign in the rearview mirror , and he brought the best of both worlds on Saturday.
After going 4-for-4 on field goals and producing Kansas City's only points against the Los Angeles Rams a week ago, Butker was a perfect 3-for-3 in the first half down in Tampa Bay. That included a 45-yard boot and a 58-yard conversion, but the true highlight was an insane 69-yarder heading into the locker room:
69-YARD FIELD GOAL TO END THE HALF 🦵 pic.twitter.com/hMfVCH2A6L
Butker came on strong after a rough open to last season, so perhaps he simply carried some of that momentum into 2026. Not all of it, though; he proceeded to doink a point-after try in the second half and also whiffed on a 43-yard field goal effort. The Chiefs will certainly embrace the highs in pressure-packed environments moving forward, but more consistency is still absolutely needed.
He was part of the reason they stuck around in this one while simultaneously contributing to the loss.
Versus the Rams, the Cyrus Allen experience stole the show despite him only having two receptions for 20 yards. He had one missed opportunity that would've been a touchdown with a bit better throw, and the training camp hype surrounding him set him up for serious buzz with a remotely productive outing. On the flip side, Jalen Royals' two receptions for 17 yards got met with mostly silence in Chiefs Kingdom. For the majority of this outing, those roles were reversed.
Allen played deep into the game, which isn't reflective of someone who's being billed by many as a pillar of the 2026 receiving room. He also failed to do much with the ball in his hands and had a low target depth. Royals, contrastly, was already at five catches for 34 yards with two minutes left in half No. 1 and showcased some unexpected wiggle after hauling in the football as the club's leading receiver overall.
This isn't a commentary on which player deserves to be WR4 more , but it was certainly interesting to see how their performances fluctuated.
Until Reid gives a legitimate reason to be concerned about 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons' back ailment, it likely isn't worth getting worked up about. Former undrafted free agent Esa Pole not looking like a starting-caliber tackle is nothing surprising, especially with him being brought along on the left side in his second season. Breaking down the other two presumed tackle options on the team, Jaylon Moore and Kahlil Benson , presents a vastly different dilemma.
Moore was already on thin ice for not nipping the right tackle "competition" in the bud and thoroughly outplaying Benson to the point of no return. It didn't help matters that he got worked over by first-round Buccaneers edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr., whom many Chiefs fans wanted to be the 2026 NFL Draft pick at ninth overall. Benson fell flat against Bain, too, and committed both a false start and an illegal formation infraction.
It was a night to forget for Moore and Benson, which can't inspire anyone until one of them rebounds.

title: Chiefs vs Bucs Preseason: Four Kansas City Players Likely to Sit
full_text:
In today's preseason matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and Tampa Bay Buccaneers , head coach Andy Reid has already ruled out several key players from the contest. Superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes remains sidelined , while other starters like Josh Simmons, Trey Smith, and Ashton Gillotte have already been ruled out with their respective injuries.
However, unlike the regular season, there is no official injury report for preseason games, leaving fans to speculate about who will suit up and who won't. But by following the team's recent practice trends and injury situations, we can get a pretty good idea of who may be unavailable. Here are four Chiefs who haven't been ruled out but are unlikely to see much action, if any, today.
After returning to the Chiefs for a second stint late in the offseason, Sneed has been dealing with a knee issue that has limited him throughout training camp. He missed the preseason opener and could be held out again today as the coaching staff takes a cautious approach.
Rookie first-round pick Mansoor Delane is another corner whose status is up in the air . He was finally cleared for full contact during padded practices earlier this week, but the Chiefs may still be hesitant to throw him into game action right away.
Unlike the other players on this list, Kelce's potential absence isn't injury-related. The coaching staff is simply easing his workload as he enters his age-37 season.
Kelce played just three snaps in last year's preseason and sat out last week's opener, so there's little reason to believe he'll suddenly see significant action today. Given his importance to the offense, the Chiefs will likely continue prioritizing his health over preseason reps.
Tranquill missed the Chiefs' first preseason game because of lingering back spasms that began bothering him two weeks ago. Linebackers Jeffrey Bassa and Jack Cochrane have received additional work in his absence. There has been no indication that Tranquill's injury will keep him out of Week 1, but the coaching staff has little reason to rush him back for a preseason contest. Don't expect to see him on the field today.
Both of Kansas City's top receivers sat out last week, although their situations are quite different. Rashee Rice is on track to receive at least some work today after dressing but not appearing in the preseason opener. Worthy's shoulder sprain, however, appears to be more concerning. The speedy wideout dealt with shoulder issues last season and admitted they hampered him throughout the 2025 campaign . With him dealing with a similar issue again, it's difficult to imagine the Chiefs risking his Week 1 availability for a handful of preseason snaps.

title: Chiefs vs. Buccaneers: NFL Preseason Preview, Score Predictions
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are back in action on Saturday, providing both the front office and coaching staffs the ability to continue assessing things. With mandatory cutdowns just over a week away, training camp has passed and tough decisions are on the horizon.
First, however, Kansas City must complete its second of three 2026 preseason games . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers await at Raymond James Stadium, having already taken down the New York Jets in the club's preseason opener. Ahead of kickoff at 6:30 p.m. CT, many are wondering which roster can flex its depth in an environment that will see numerous players fighting for jobs.
How might Saturday's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 2 of the preseason.
Joshua Brisco: With injuries to Ashton Gillotte , Josh Simmons and Trey Smith, this game should provide valuable opportunities for a few defensive ends and offensive linemen to make an impact against—potentially—some of the Buccaneers’ starters.
I’m hoping to see a healthy dose of Kahlil Benson at right tackle and R Mason Thomas and Felix Anudike-Uzomah on the edge. However, as long as the games don’t matter, I'm not picking the Chiefs to win a preseason game until they break the streak!
Jordan Foote: In this one, I'm keeping an eye on which players can respond to standout performances from a week ago. That goes in both directions, as defensive backfield stoppers Nohl Williams and Jaden Hicks were excellent but offensive pieces like wideout Jason Brownlee and tackle Ethan Driskell struggled immensely.
This outing could go a long way in helping the coaching staff iron out its eventual 53-man roster. Although the Bucs' ground game fell flat against the New York Jets to open the preseason, this remains an offense with ample depth. It might just be enough to squeak by the visitors. Let's roll with a one-score game in which neither team looks particularly impressive in a grind-it-out style of bout.
Joshua Schulman: Despite some strong individual performances in the preseason opener, the Chiefs’ offensive effort against the Rams was subpar as they failed to muster up a touchdown. It doesn’t feel like we’ll be watching a shootout this week either, considering how impressive the defense looked last week before it fell apart in the fourth quarter.
The Bucs appear to have found a star in the making in quarterback Jalon Daniels, who showed far more promise than fellow rookie Garrett Nussmeier a week ago. Behind a banged-up KC offensive line that committed nine penalties last week, it’s likely going to be another underwhelming offensive showing for Andy Reid and Co.
Tyler Brown: With the Bucs expected to play their starters and Andy Reid traditionally giving starters their most runway in second preseason games, there should be much more to glean from this week. There's no Patrick Mahomes again, nor is there Smith or Simmons, but that just means there will finally be an extended runway for both Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore at the tackle spots.
On defense, Jaden Hicks replicating last week's performance will be something to watch, along with what flashes we see from the Chiefs' rookie class . I expect KC to be successful on the ground again. The only question is whether it can find a way to finish drives in the end zone.

title: 4 Options After Chargers Reveal Final Tyler Biadasz Injury News
full_text:
It’s officially over for Tyler Biadasz and the Los Angeles Chargers in 2026.
The Chargers were trying to hold out hope that Biadasz might be able to return later in the 2026 season after recovering from a serious knee injury.
In the wake of the Chargers’ second preseason game, though, the team put an end to that with the reveal that Biadasz will move to injured reserve.
The crusher: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , Biadasz “exhausted all options before the move was made. Likely meaning, no return is possible.
So, where do the Chargers go from here?
The Chargers drafted Slaughter to play guard, despite being a college center. He’s back at center now and will stay there. Barring a shocker, he’s the unquestioned starter. But his reps in preseason Week 2 were up-and-down, as expected.
More concerning, at least for now, is just who might actually emerge at left guard, where at least three names still appear to have a chance at starting there.
Now 32 years old, Daniel Brunskill spent last year with Miami. That wasn’t his only connection to Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, either, given his years in San Francisco from 2019-2022. Right now, he’s currently with Washington, but it’s an option worth exploring as a backup if he doesn’t make it through final cuts or winds up on the trade block.
Graham Glasgow and James Daniels are two veterans with the ability to play multiple spots on the interior of an offensive line.
Glasgow is 34 years old and spent the last few years in Detroit. He’d need to be willing to accept a backup and mentor-type role behind Slaughter, though.
Similar story for Daniels, who happened to spend last year in Miami, but saw his three-year deal become just one after an injury derailed things. He’s still 28 years old, but would need to accept a spot behind Slaughter.
Because of the absolute mess that is left guard, this is an extremely uncomfortable place for the Chargers to be right now. Finding a backup center isn’t that big of a deal. Neither is starting a rookie center, provided the veterans around him are reliable.
But left guard is a question mark, right guard always felt a little unaddressed with Cole Strange and Rashawn Slater has already had a minor injury setback at a tackle spot. Instead of the best-ever line with a flashy new coordinator, the conversation shifts to whether the line can even be better than last year’s unit.

title: Chargers Training Camp Problem Might be Going From Bad to Worse
full_text:
Roughly one week into the preseason, perhaps the biggest problem the Los Angeles Chargers faced was just who might end up at one of the starting guard spots in front of Justin Herbert.
Fast forward to now, it’s almost a red-button emergency situation.
The fallout from the Tyler Biadasz injury is immense. Rookie Jake Slaughter now has to kick back to center, leaving a mess of things for the Chargers to figure out at left guard.
Making matters even worse, the backup offensive line spots don’t seem so hot , either. Keep in mind that’s with the Chargers adding free agents for Mike McDaniel and spending four of their eight draft picks on linemen.
Time is running out for the Chargers to show signs of life in that area.
With Biadasz down, Slaughter, the rookie center drafted to play guard, has kicked back to center. The four or so names still involved in the left guard battle aren’t exactly standing out one way or another.
Just look at updates from ESPN’s Kris Rhim , who said the first practice after the preseason beatdown at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers “was one of the worst days for the offense.”
Rhim noted that Justin Herbert threw one interception and multiple turnover-worthy passes beyond that. Slaughter struggled against the likes of Jamaree Caldwell and that overall it was a bad day for the line.
All that while shuffling things around in a big way. Rashawn Slater briefly returned to practice after his apparent setback. Otherwise, Travis Burke and Trey Pipkins rotated at left tackle. But Pipkins started the day at left guard before giving way to Kayode Awosika.
There’s really just…nobody emerging at guard. The fact Pipkins, the primary backup swing tackle, keeps getting first-team reps there, probably isn’t a good sign. Awosika is a mid-tier free-agent add who isn’t establishing himself there.
Keep in mind that Branson Taylor, a former practice squad member last year, has been one of the biggest “breakouts” of training camp. His rise has been surprising and it could very well end up being him as the starter in Week 1. But with how things have been going, one has to wonder if perhaps his rise is, at least in part, a result of so much uncertainty and middling competition at guard.
None of this is to say anything about Cole Strange, who most agreed was a pretty questionable, non-challengeable signing as a starter at right guard by McDaniel. He’s been up-and-down at times and will now need to line up next to a rookie center.
It would be one thing if the Chargers were simply seeing a rookie center go through growing pains. But the fact there’s still a left guard competition next to him right before the third preseason game and no reliable way to get a good player in the door in a lineman-starved NFL is a panic-worthy thing.

title: Injury Updates, Offensive Line Sparks Concerns, Chargers Try to Recover at Practice
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers returned to practice on Saturday while still licking their wound from an embarrassing night of football on Thursday night against the 49ers. The team seemed to have taken the loss of Tyler Biadasz due to a major knee injury as a punch to the gut that they have yet to recover from.
Practices are no longer open to the public and therefore news and highlights will be limited but there is still plenty to go over from Saturday's return to the Bolt. Let's dive into news and questions about the Chargers from Saturday's practice.
The Chargers had several starters return to practice in some capacity on Saturday. Left tackle Rashawn Slater, wide receivers Tre' Harris and Quentin Johnston, cornerbacks Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson all were on the field on Saturday
The following players were sidelined due to injuries: Tight End Scott Matlock (who was wearing a walking boot on the sidelines during the loss to the 49ers) Edge rusher Bud Dupree Edge rusher Kyle Kennard Offensive lineman Branson Taylor Wide receiver Brenen Thompson Cornerback Eric Rogers
The status of center Tyler Biadasz still has yet to be labeled or updated in regards to whether he will be put on injured reserve and miss the entire 2026 season or if there is a chance at a last season comeback.
Defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell left practice early and was working with trainers off to the side.
Rashawn Slater's return to practice included individual drills and one session of 11-on-11 team period. Head coach Jim Harbaugh made it clear at his pre-practice press conference that Slater would be ramping back up to full practice. Slater exited practice following the first team period and watched from the sideline.
Jim Harbaugh said it himself, "The film did not lie. I mean, we got beat and beat ourselves as a team in all three phases." The most concerning part of the Chargers offense from joint practice, through the game and even Saturday's practice, is rooted in the offensive line. The interior of the offensive line, when the starters were in, got routinely beat whether is pass protection or run blocking.
The offensive line woes could be directly tied to the lack of continuity between Jake Slaughter and the guards next to him after he was thrust into the starting role. Slaughter's move to center, his natural position, removes him from the left guard competition. Branson Taylor was sidelined today and instead of Kayode Awosika getting valuable reps next to Slaughter, Trey Pipkins was the first left guard in team period with Rashawn Slater's return.
Roster cutdown day is a week away and the Chargers are still not settled on their starting offensive line. They have three weeks to gel and work together but Harbaugh has indicated they are not close to naming a starter. For a team that gave up historic levels of pressure up the middle in 2025, fans' frustration with the process and the current results is understandable.
It remains to be seen if the front office smashes the panic button and makes a trade for a depth piece with starting potential. ESPN's Kris Rhim covers the Chargers and his practice notes may have been clearly indicative over the levels of concern facing the Chargers. His first note of the day said "It was one of the worst days for the offense. Interior offensive line struggled, and the passing offense wasn't great."

title: The Chargers Rookie Nobody Expected to be Talking About
full_text:
The NFL preseason is full of players trying to turn a few weeks of football into an opportunity that can change their careers instantly. Many players come and go during training camp. However for a undrafted rookie in Los Angeles, an opportunity on the 53-man roster has started to look very real.
Jacob Spomer entered Los Angeles Chargers training camp without the same spotlight that followed some of the team’s draft picks. He wasn’t selected during the 2026 NFL draft, and there was no guarantee he would make enough of an impression to stick around.
But so far, he’s giving the Chargers plenty to think about. With the offensive line dealing with multiple injuries, Spomer could be a legit depth piece for the Bolts. Based off recent seasons and the offensive line woes, this addition is more important than ever.
Throughout training camp, Jacob Spomer has continued to receive opportunities at center and has looked comfortable handling the responsibility . He has been able to work with different combinations along the offensive line, giving the coaching staff a closer look at what he can provide. As of right now, he looks to be a very promising player. For an undrafted player, those reps are important. Every practice gives him another chance to show that he belongs.
Spomer's training camp has been solid, being reliable and improving every day. He seems to be beating expectations at a rapid speed. The biggest positive came from last Thursday's game, where he performed very well.
The center posted a 82.6 percent pass blocking rate , with zero sacks or pressures, according to Pro Football Focus. That statistic shows how steady he is in pass protection. We all know what happened last year when Herbert thew the ball. Spomer could be a perfect piece for the line in the future.
The Tyler Biadasz injury was heartbreaking to hear, and was a punch in the gut for the Chargers. This makes the timing of Spomer's recent breakout especially important. The need for a serviceable center depth-wise, has become a sudden topic of discussion. Spomer's ability to step in when needed, protect the quarterback, and handle pressure can give Los Angeles another option. His recent success does not mean much, as many things are up in the air. However, it should make you feel better about the future of the offense.

title: 1 Great and 1 Not-So-Great Chargers Injury Development at Training Camp
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers were on the receiving end of a beatdown at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2 of the preseason.
Sent home to lick wounds and regroup, the Chargers reemerged for Day 17 of training camp practice seeking answers across an offensive line that is receiving some major negative reviews right now.
Assemingling the Chargers final 53-man roster isn’t going to be easy, to say the least.
Here’s a quick rundown of good and bad injury developments at camp.
There was some major speculation about whether Slater would see a snap of live-action practice at all before the regular season. He suffered some sort of mysterious injury setback near the start of camp. That naturally created some concerns about his health one year removed from his torn patellar tendon suffered during last year’s camp.
No telling if the Chargers will risk Slater at all in live sessions and especially preseason action, but the fact he’s back is good news.
The post-Tyler Biadasz injury shakeup is limping along.
Jake Slaughter, a center drafted to play guard, is now back as the starter center at with Biadasz on the shelf. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is talking it up with reporters, at least.
"Jake Slaughter is now our starting center, so that's a big change," Harbaugh said, according to Eric Smith of Chargers.com . "The center position, right guard, right tackle, left tackle … those four [are set]."
Harbaugh added this about the outlook for final cuts: "Whether we have nine offensive linemen, 10, 11, on the final roster, they're all in the mix for roles," Harbaugh continued. "Starting roles and backup role."
A rookie making a transition back to another position on the fly just before the season is concerning enough.
But the left guard spot Slaughter has left is a mess.
Let Harbaugh tell it, Kayode Awosika is the leader there. But Saturday’s practice started with Trey Pipkins running with the ones. Branson Taylor remains in the mix, too.
So, the competition for left guard includes:
That’s not to say the Chargers can easily go out and find capable help. There’s going to be some reliance on offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel to scheme around any issues up front.
But with Slater shaky, a rookie at center and two new, questionable starters at guards, there’s plenty of cause for concern about the line in front of Justin Herbert for Week 1.

title: Chargers Injuries, Preseason Week 2 Reshape 53-Man Roster Prediction
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers exit preseason Week 2 with more questions than answers.
Tyler Biadasz is lost to injury . Jim Harbaugh is mad at a punter while much bigger problems chase the roster into another week of training camp.
And that old problem, the interior of the offensive line?
Here’s a quick rundown of an updated Chargers 53-man roster projection that attempts to account for some of the big changes about to go down.
DJ Uiagalelei has suddenly made some noise in the backup quarterback competition behind Justin Herbert. It’s not enough to say he knocks Trey Lance off the roster just yet, but something to watch.
Amar Johnson has had a really strong preseason when the line in front of the backs looks fit for pro play. But if they can only keep three, the Chargers will go with Kimani Vidal.
Good luck figuring out the order of who sees the field for snaps and when. Oronde Gadsden almost seems like he’s been passed up. Either way, the top three are very obvious.
It’s tough to leave Keandre Lambert-Smith off the list. The Chargers already moved on from someone like Luke Grimm. And the rookie Brenen Thompson can account for returns/gadget stuff that would have gone to Derius Davis. But it’s still very much a heated competition.
We’ll call Tyler Biadasz an IR for now. Kayode Awosika is the leader at left guard now that Jake Slaughter has moved over to center. Travis Burke is a breakout backup swing tackle.
Not really much to say here. Teair Tart is the leader they signed to an extension this offseason, then added Dalvin Tomlinson in free agency.
Undrafted free agent Nadame Tucker has lived up to the fanbase’s hype and should make the final roster based on what’s happened so far. The last spot goes to Kyle Kennard in the hopes he can still reach some of his own draft slotting, pushing Bud Dupree out.
Maybe the most boring position here, which is a good thing. We get a little bold by pushing Junior Colson off the final 53 after his struggles to meet expectations. Guys like Marlowe Wax are just too consistently good.
Years of fantastic drafting and overall value finds have led to this point. Donte Jackson is a great veteran to start, Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart were strong mid-round picks and late values like Nikko Reed double as good depth with intriguing long-term upside.
Rookie draft pick Genesis Smith has a real shot at playing time here, provided he can prove in live-game action that he’s grown past tackling woes. It’s a good problem to have for the Chargers at a strong spot.

title: Jim Harbaugh’s Mad at a Punter But the Chargers Have Much Bigger Problems
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers got blown out of the water during the preseason loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
Exiting the humbling, one of the bigger talking points was Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh taking aim at punter JK Scott.
Scott allowed a touchdown return by the 49ers on a poor all-around play from the unit, capped off with a whiff from the punter himself:
JACOB COWING WITH THE 83-YARD PUNT RETURN TD 🏠 SFvsLAC on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/BUV9YE8LyF
“The punt was short and in the middle, and then we got out-flanked,” Harbaugh said . “No, he’s got to have a plan when he’s in that position to make the tackle. Something we need to work on, coach up.”
A terrible all-around day for the Chargers, no doubt, but considering the other big problem, the punter mistake that resembles the day as a whole is the least of Harbaugh’s worries right now.
Deja vu time: The interior of the offensive line is a problem.
One year removed from the Mekhi Becton disaster and years of Bradley Bozeman, the Chargers are a mess up front for Justin Herbert yet again.
The Tyler Biadasz injury didn’t help, obviously. He was supposed to be the veteran lynchpin in the middle. Now, rookie Jake Slaughter, the guy drafted to transition to guard, will stick at center and start there.
Things…didn’t go all that great. Granted, Herbert played three snaps and the offense is vanilla. But the college center going through growing pains was obvious.
More concerning is actually guard. At the left spot, it’s going to be veteran journeyman Kayode Awosika or Branson Taylor, a former practice squad member last year who has enjoyed a strong summer.
Nobody at the left guard spot really looked that great. And at right guard, where former mid-tier starter Cole Strange sits after coming over via free agency…didn’t look all that hot either:
Look at this 4 straight play sequence by RG Cole Strange man… https://t.co/DtWyZKZYNt pic.twitter.com/xQmXGlX0YB
The Chargers are too far into things right now to magically go out and find more starting-caliber competition at guard. And with Biadasz out, center and the depth behind Slaughter are actually an even bigger concern.
So, once again, the Chargers have perhaps the best offensive tackle duo in the NFL with Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. But Slater is dealing with an injury and how many reps he’ll see before the season remains to be seen. And having that duo is great, but they can only do so much if the interior is a weak point yet again.
Fair game on Harbaugh for calling out a punter who probably should have had even more heat on him for a roster spot earlier this offseason. But the organization's repeated lazy efforts on the interior of the offensive line while hoarding cap space could come back to bite them in a way that even the hyped Mike McDaniel can’t save.

title: Latest Update Provides New Insight Into the Chargers' Offensive Line Injuries
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are at the final stretch of the preseason, with more questions surrounding one specific position. Similar to last year, the injuries are already starting to pile up on the offensive front. The injuries have created plenty of uncertainty for a team that was hoping to enter the regular season with a more stable offensive line. The nightmare continues as players keep dropping, weakening the line even more.
With that being said, the Chargers received yet another update on center Tyler Biadasz , as well as star left tackle Rashawn Slater.
The latest update from ESPN insider Adam Schefter gives the Chargers a small reason for optimism, especially when it comes to Rashawn Slater. Schefter reported that Slater is expected to return to practice this weekend , which would be an important step for a Chargers offensive line that has already taken several hits. Getting their star left tackle back on the practice field would give Los Angeles a chance to see how he is progressing before the regular season begins.
The news surrounding Tyler Biadasz however, remains much more concerning. Schefter reported that the veteran center is out indefinitely after suffering an ACL injury, although there is still some hope that he could potentially return later in the season. In most cases similar to this one, the center will have the best chance of returning if the Chargers make a deep playoff run.
As Schefter stated, “There’s hope that maybe he could come back later this season.” That possibility is far from a guarantee, but it gives the Chargers something to hold onto while Biadasz continues to receive additional medical evaluations . With Slater potentially returning to practice and Biadasz facing an uncertain recovery. The Chargers’ offensive line remains a major storyline heading into the regular season.
. @AdamSchefter provides an update on the injuries for two key members on the Chargers' offensive line ✍️ pic.twitter.com/bSa39Ayide
The latest update provides new insight for the Chargers, painting a clearer but uncertain picture heading into the regular season. With Biadasz out for the season most likey and Rashawn Slater up in the air, we can only hope the Bolts can make the correct adjustments to protect their franchise quarterback. Most fans will not want to see another repeat of last year, but things seem to be spiraling out of control.
All in all, the Chargers have the talent and depth to salvage this line, even with roadblocks in their way. With correct execution, this season might not be over before it starts.

title: Chargers Roster Spotlights: Josh Harris & Peter Bowden, A Young Prodigy and Legendary Veteran
full_text:
Josh Harris, born on April 27, 1989, in Fulda, Germany, played his high school ball at Carrollton High School, where he was a three-sport athlete, playing in football, wrestling and baseball. Unfortunately, Harris was not heavily recruited, being a zero-star recruit , according to 247Sports.
Even with this, Harris was able to enroll at Auburn, fighting for the team's long snapper job. He finally would play in 2009 earning four tackles in 13 games, then winning the BCS National Championship alongside Cam Newton in 2010. 2011 was Harris' final season with the program, earning three tackles as the team
Harris would go undrafted following the 2012 NFL Draft, finding himself with the Atlanta Falcons competing for a roster spot. He would win the spot and spend the next ten seasons with the team, helping the team make it to the infamous 2016 Super Bowl.
Harris also earned a Pro Bowl and Second-Team All-Pro honors in 2021, right before he was eligible for a contract extension.
The Bolts' saw the All-Pro veteran on the market and signed him to a then-market resetting contract, in hopes of him bolstering their weak special teams unit. Harris would do exactly such, continuing his dominance as one of the league's best long snappers, turning around the Chargers special teams unit.
This was especially seen when Harris went down with injury in 2025, missing nine games. Fans instantly saw his impact when he was replaced by long snappers found off the streets of NFL free agency.
