title: Steelers Need to Have Kick Returner Replacement Ready
full_text:
As inconceivable as it was even a matter of weeks ago, Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Kaden Wetjen might be on thin ice.
On the penultimate play of the first quarter, the fourth-round pick fumbled on a punt return and nearly handed the New York Jets fantastic field position at the Steelers ' 31-yard line.
Wetjen was bailed out after it was ruled that New York was out-of-bounds before it gained possession of the ball upon recovering it. That doesn't mean it wasn't still a huge mistake for him, however.
Head coach Mike McCarthy didn't shy away from delivering a pointed evaluation of where Wetjen stood earlier in the week either, telling reporters that, "we've got to get him to clean up his everyday stuff, the mental errors."
Wetjen's 74-yard catch and five-yard touchdown in the preseason opener led to some intensified optimism surrounding his offensive impact, but with no catches against the Jets and with McCarthy clearly asking for more from him, it's hard to feel confident in where he stands at the moment.
If Wetjen doesn't work out as a return man, and it's still far too early to know whether or not that'll be the case, who could Pittsburgh turn to as his replacement(s)?
Both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle have experience returning kicks as recently as the 2025 campaign, with the former going for 205 yards on eight attempts while the latter posted 197 yards on eight returns last year.
Warren is currently listed as the second-team kick returner while Dowdle is the second-team punt returner and third-team kick returner on Pittsburgh's depth chart .
Should the Steelers try and avoid giving either of their top two running backs too heavy of a workload in that department, perhaps Roman Wilson could emerge as a punt return option after putting in some work in that role throughout training camp this summer.
Another running back in Travis Homer, who has a real shot of making the 53-man roster, has returned 19 kicks for 473 yards and a touchdown during his NFL career. Just two of those tries have come since the beginning of the 2021 campaign, though.
The issue there is that Homer has been the personal protector on the punt team, and Pittsburgh may not want to pull him out of that spot so that he can return punts instead.
Seventh-round rookie Eli Heidenreich is increasingly unlikely to crack the 53-man roster.
In a scenario where Wetjen's handle on the return man duties is relinquished, however, Heidenreich would immediately become a prime candidate to take over in his place.
The Navy product and Pittsburgh native only returned nine kicks with one fair catch on a punt during his time in college, but he worked as a return man during training camp and has the tools to potentially thrive in that role.
Max Hurleman, who's on the wrong side of the roster bubble and returned a combined 62 kicks and punts throughout his college career, would be another name to watch. He brought back two kicks for 58 yards alongside a punt for 14 yards against the Jets  and has some juice back there that could be worth tapping into for the Steelers.
D'Shawn Jamison also doesn't have much of a case to make the 53-man roster as of now. He did rack up 1,435 yards and two touchdowns across 53 kick returns during his time at Texas to go with 362 yards and a score on 44 punt returns, though, so if he makes the practice squad and is elevated or if he eventually signs to the active roster, he could make a splash too.

title: Same Problem Returning for Steelers' Roman Wilson
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Disappointment is the first word that comes to mind when evaluating the Pittsburgh Steelers' second preseason game against the New York Jets.
From quarterbacks to the line, every member of the Steelers offense looked out of sorts and discombobulated. Calling anyone from that contest a standout player would be disingenuous.
For young players like quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar, those struggles are expected and embraced. It's one thing to watch Eli Heidenreich make a mistake or Doneiko Slaughter take an ill-timed penalty. The big problem is when veterans who are supposed to be integral pieces of the regular season roster flash warning signs. Unfortunately for wide receiver Roman Wilson, that same problem returned against the Jets.
The monster reared its ugly head for Wilson. Over his first two seasons, it felt like Wilson was undeservedly in former head coach Mike Tomlin's doghouse. But after watching his performance against the Jets, maybe Tomlin's frustrations were warranted.
Wilson is an excellent athlete and hard worker, but his mastery of the position leaves so much to be desired. He doesn't recognize the small nuances and differences in coverages and situations, and because of that inability, he often puts himself in poor positions to help the offense.
This is precisely what happened during Howard's first interception of the game. As the team was driving downfield, Wilson worked a route across the middle of the field, Instead of moving toward the incoming pass intended for him, Wilson drifted toward the endzone and waited for the ball to come to him.
As a result, the creeping safety was able to read the play and jump the route. Howard made a poor throw, but Wilson did his quarterback no favors in the process.
The second interception truly lies on Wilson, in my opinion. Once again working against man coverage, Wilson's speed allowed him to gain a bit of separation, but instead of keeping his route perpendicular to the sidelines, he once again drifted upfield. The same criticism against Howard's first interception can be levied against him in this instance as well, as he should have led his receiver more. Once again, however, Wilson's sloppy route-running contributed to the turnover.
The Steelers enter the 2026 season with the expectation that they have more weapons for quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and Wilson was a key part of that. As the third receiver on the depth chart behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., the offense is expected to take a significant leap in the coming campaign.
But if Wilson doesn't run routes with the precision Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy demand, he will quickly find himself relegated to the sidelines once more.
And that means the Steelers are again looking around for answers at the wide receiver position. Rookie Germie Bernard, the team's recent second-round draft pick, has looked like a polished professional in his first game action. That skill and confidence clashes with Rodgers' historical reliance on veteran receivers. Something has to give for the Pittsburgh offense, and Wilson could have made that decision so much easier.
As the preseason wraps up, the same issues are already emerging for Roman Wilson . It's a shame for the former third-round pick, because the talent and drive are clearly there. So too, is a flashing warning sign that McCarthy and the Steelers can't ignore.

title: Steelers Have a Massive Problem They Need to Fix
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The left side of the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive line found their way in the second preseason game . Left tackle Troy Fautanu was already back to his All-Pro form, Mason McCormick has transitioned well to the left guard position, and Zach Frazier is, well, Zach Frazier.
The right side, however, looked even worse than they did in the preseason opener. Dylan Cook, the starting right tackle, has lost rep after rep in two appearances. Spencer Anderson has been up-and-down in his snaps, but neither has assured head coach Mike McCarthy that they can anchor the strong side of the offensive line. McCarthy rotated in Brock Hoffman and Broderick Jones during the first half, showing that he hasn't quite made up his mind when it comes to that tandem.
It's fair that McCarthy hasn't made up his mind. How could he? The options are grim right now, regardless of if you're discussing the starter or going further down the depth chart. With just one game separating this team from the regular season, the Steelers have a growing and concerning problem at right tackle.
It might be a bit dramatic, seeing as he hasn't played a game in the NFL yet, but the Steelers' final hope is first-round rookie Max Iheanachor. The 21st overall pick in the 2026 draft had the starting RT job nearly stolen from Cook, but an injury suffered early in training camp derailed his early ascension.
But now, the Steelers are being forced to rely on the inexperienced Iheanachor as the starter on the offensive line opposite Fautanu.
That's a tall order for Iheanachor. Not because he doesn't have what it takes, but because the pressure is quickly turning all the way up in Pittsburgh. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers and company want to make a legitimate run for the Lombardi Trophy. In order to get there, they need to solve this right tackle issue. Iheanachor is currently their best, and perhaps only, remaining in-house option.
With the Steelers and general manager Omar Khan, the trade market can never be discounted. They've taken multiple big swings via trade over the past few seasons, and with the team all-in for the 2026 campaign, it might make sense to dial the phones once again.
The only problem is that the Steelers might not have a willing trade partner right now. Teams are still deciding on their final 53-man rosters ahead of the regular season, and some teams might not be willing to part with anyone while they figure things out. By the time they are, who knows what type of return they will seek for a starting-caliber tackle.
For the Steelers, the trade market is a dangerous route to pursue.
There is one last resort the Steelers could pivot to, but admittedly, it doesn't inspire confidence or represent an obvious upgrade. A few free agents are still available on the open market, and could be a short-term solution while Iheanachor makes his way back to 100%.
One player is former Cincinnati Bengals first-round pick, Jonah Williams. He was a solid tackle in Cincinnati before injuries derailed his past two seasons with the Arizona Cardinals. The last thing the Steelers need is another quasi-healthy right tackle in the mix, but if he had a clean bill of health, he brings 74 games of starting experience to a needy position.
Another player with starting experience who could be had for cheap is former Cleveland Browns lineman Jack Conklin. With 114 starts over his NFL career with the Browns and Tennessee Titans, he would be a true veteran mentor for Iheanachor and Fautanu. Injuries are also a concern for Conklin, but if the Steelers are desperate enough, he might be worth a shot.

title: 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Steelers Loss to Jets
full_text:
After blowing out the Green Bay Packers in the first game of the preseason by a score of 28-9, the Pittsburgh Steelers were on the other side of a beatdown this time around.
The New York Jets walked into Acrisure Stadium and dominated the Steelers at every turn, resulting in a shutout 17-0 loss for the latter. Pittsburgh cleaned up the penalties after they were a major issue vs. Green Bay, but the offensive line floundered once again while the unit as a whole went 5-of-16 on third downs.
With that, here are five winners and six losers from the contest for the Steelers.
Regardless of if he is a 53-man roster lock or not , Howard did himself zero favors against the Jets.
The 24-year-old had some flashes, including a 16-yard strike to Ben Skowronek for a first down in New York territory, but he followed it up a few plays later with his first of two interceptions on the night.
Howard's lack of standout arm strength was evident on both of his picks, and overall it was a game to forget for the former sixth-round pick as his hopes of winning the backup quarterback job over Mason Rudolph seem all but dashed.
Bruener is a key component of Pittsburgh's special teams units, but he appears to be making some strides on the defensive side of the ball as well.
The inside linebacker logged just one defensive snap as a rookie last season. After logging a pass breakup and a sack on back-to-back plays during the Jets' final drive of the first half, however, Bruener is starting to prove that he can hold his own on that side of the ball.
Jones had a real rough go of it against New York. Whether it was David Bailey crushing him for a sack on 3rd-and-9 with a little under five minutes to go in the first quarter or Nate Lynn logging a sack of his own on him in the fourth quarter, the 2023 first-rounder's struggles were on full display as he took on another heavy workload.
It was never going to be pretty for Jones while building back his strength after suffering a significant neck injury last November that required spinal fusion surgery.
That doesn't excuse his poor play, though, and there have to be some serious questions about his viability moving forward.
Compared to most of his Steelers teammates, Sawyer has little to play for in the preseason when it comes to securing a larger role, considering he's set as the team's No. 4 EDGE rusher.
Still, Sawyer went out there and made his presence known with some impressive stops against the run all while registering a sack of Cade Klubnik at the end of the first half.
Though the Jets failed to gain possession on the sideline, Wetjen's fumble on a kick return during the closing seconds of the first quarter was simply inexcusable.
The fourth-round rookie also didn't have a single target or catch at wide receiver a week after posting 79 yards and a touchdown, putting him in somewhat of a treacherous spot leading into the preseason finale against the Buffalo Bills.
McCarthy made it a point to challenge Wetjen while talking to the media this week by stating, "We've got to get him to clean up his everyday stuff, the mental errors," but the Iowa product didn't rise to the challenge vs. New York.
Jenkins played like he knew his chances of cracking Pittsburgh's 53-man roster were on the line.
The 32-year-old, who's entering the 10th season of his career, was all over the field and caused a ton of pressure while being utilized as a blitzer by defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.
From forcing an intentional grounding call on Klubnik to finishing with two quarterback hits and making plays against the run, Jenkins' stock is pointing upwards.
Driscoll, in all likelihood, was never going to make the Steelers' 53-man roster.
For a veteran with 18 starts and nearly 1,500 offensive snaps under his belt, however, he looked surprisingly unpolished as he gave up a sack and generally was beat far too often in pass protection throughout the contest.
A practice squad candidate who wasn't exactly stout vs. Green Bay either, Driscoll has been a disappointment so far this preseason.
After signing a one-year deal last week to return to Pittsburgh following a one-year stopover with the Las Vegas Raiders, where he played for Graham, Roberts reminded everyone why he has the potential to be such a force in the middle of the defense.
The 32-year-old single-handedly wrecked New York's initial offensive series of the second half, showing off his recognition skills against the run before clicking and closing into the flats to stop the Jets one yard short of a first down on 4th-and-3.
The fact that he remained on the field through the fourth quarter was surprising to say the least, but Roberts made the most of the opportunity.
Not only did Spears-Jennings force an incompletion with a big hit on Jets running back Sam Scott halfway through the third quarter, but he also drew a block in the back penalty while serving as a gunner on Pittsburgh's punt team.
The seventh-round rookie was one of the stories of training camp for the Steelers, and that's carried over to the preseason thus far.

title: Time to Say Goodbye to Steelers' Will Howard
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers gave second-year quarterback Will Howard the golden opportunity he's been waiting for. In the team's second preseason game against the New York Jets, Howard started and worked with the first-team offense. The hope was that he would prove he was ready to leapfrog Mason Rudolph and assume backup duty responsibilites.
That's not quite how things turned out for the Steelers' 2025 sixth-round draft pick. The crowd at Acrisure Stadium provided a hero's welcome, but the on-field performance didn't live up to the hype.
Instead, Howard may have played himself out a job in Pittsburgh.
Credit to the young quarterback, who called out his own disappointing performance after the team's 17-0 loss to the Jets.
"Things to learn from. Just the performance wasn't up to par," he said. "It's a shame because those were both good drives and I thought we were moving the ball really well. And one of the first things we talk about is protecting the football... Just gotta be better and learn from it."
Howard has never lacked intelligence or the professionalism that many covet for the starting quarterback position. If only that were the determining factor in making the Steelers' 53-man roster, but the on-field performance speaks for itself. He finished the game 10-of-15 passing, throwing two interceptions. One was a characteristic turnover from a young quarterback who failed to read the defense correctly.
The second one is up for debate regarding who is responsible, but the fact remains that he failed to lead any touchdown drives in a start he absolutely needed to deliver. As a result, his chances of making the roster have hit rock bottom.
The Steelers have been toying with the potential of keeping four quarterbacks on the roster.
That possibility and line of thinking have likely ended after the second preseason game. It's not all Howard's fault, and he was far from the only player who struggled. The problem is that no one was under more pressure to perform well.
Howard wasn't able to seal the deal, and he might be looking for a new NFL franchise. There is, however, a small chance that he can redeem himself in the preseason finale.
The team will likely play both youngsters against the Buffalo Bills, much like they did against the Jets. If Howard is given the chance to start again, he can salvage his chances in Pittsburgh. He'd have to be picture-perfect, but it would be his last chance to continue playing for the Steelers.

title: 4 Winners & 4 Losers in Seahawks Preseason Week 2 Loss vs. Titans
full_text:
After a loss to Dallas in Week 1, the Seattle Seahawks were on the road for the second week of the NFL preseason. The Seahawks went into Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans in a prime-time game on Sunday night.
Once again, the majority of the starters were out, including rookie running back Jadarian Price. The first-round pick didn't play against the Cowboys, and fans were hopeful to see his debut on Sunday. We learned early in the day that wouldn't happen, as Seattle said Price would sit the entire preseason .
As for the game itself, Seattle was in control until the final quarter, which is when Tennessee scored a late touchdown to take a 19-16 lead, which wound up being the final. With this game behind us, let's see who stands out as both winners and loser from Week 2 of the preseason.
Undrafted out of Utah in 2025, Connor O'Toole appeared in eight games as a rookie and had five tackles. He's a long shot to make the team this year, but he made a strong case for himself against the Titans. O'Toole was active all night and broke through the line to record 1.5 sacks.
It was all Seattle in the first half, but the Titans were given life late in the second quarter. The Seahawks forced a punt, but Cody White was unable to track the ball as the returner and fumbled it away. Tennessee recovered the ball at the Seattle 11. The defense held, but White still gave the Titans three points for free.
Veteran linebacker Chazz Surratt is fighting for a roster spot after playing in 11 games for the Seahawks last year. On Sunday, he made an excellent play, chasing down Cam Ward and recording a strip-sack.
Great hustle by Chazz Surratt! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fCfwXy09Rm
Surratt finished with five tackles and one sack, doing much of his damage against the Titans' starters.
With Jake Bobo suffering an injury earlier this week, there's an open spot at wide receiver. Ricky White III has all the tools to take that job, but made a costly mistake late in this one. After surrendering the lead in the fourth quarter, White made a third-down reception for 30 yards, but the play didn't count. White was flagged for offensive pass interference, putting the Seahawks in a third-and-15 situation.
A second-round pick in 2025, Elijah Arroyo joined the Seahawks with plenty of promise but didn't reach his potential as a rookie. This year, he has looked like a vastly improved player during camp and had a great night against the Titans. Arroyo wasn't on the field long, but made an impact with 50 yards on two receptions, including a 36-yard touchdown.
Drew Lock ➡️ Elijah Arroyo for a Seahawks TD! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mpb74cucFq
Arroyo was the No. 2 tight end in 2025 with AJ Barner having a breakout season. Don't be surprised if the sophomore begins to eat into his targets as he continues to develop.
Jason Myers has been one of the league's most consistent kickers and went 41-of-48 in 2025. There shouldn't be any reason for long-term concern, but Myers had a rough night on Sunday. He missed an extra point and field goal in the first half. Even his first make, which was a 48-yarder during the second quarter, only narrowly snuck in.
With Price and George Holani out, Jacardia Wright was given a chance to shine, and that's exactly what he did. The second-year player put a lot of pressure on players ahead of him, most notably Emanuel Wilson, by rushing for 81 yards on eight attempts. The big play was a 69-yard touchdown in the first quarter that led to an explosion of excitement from the sidelines .
Jacardia Wright takes it straight to the end zone for a 69-yard TD 🗣️ SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bVuJlpcBGS
You would have liked to see more on the remainder of his carries, but Wright did enough to insert himself into the conversation at running back.
Jalen Milroe has more than enough talent to compete for the QB2 spot with Drew Lock, but he still hasn't put it all together. Sunday was a perfect example of this as he had some great plays, including a 16-yard run. He also had two interceptions, including one to end a potential game-winning drive. In all, he was 6-of-11 for 52 yards and was sacked twice. Not an ideal outing for the sophomore.

title: Seahawks Rookie Bud Clark Suffers Injury vs. Titans
full_text:
The preseason is a good tool for teams that want to see some of their younger players get some snaps in a live game. The results don't matter, but the injury risk is still there, which is why the Seattle Seahawks went into their Week 2 meeting with their starters on the bench.
Early in their game against the Tennessee Titans , Seattle was reminded of the risk as one of their top rookies went down with an injury to his right leg. It didn't take long for the training staff to bring out an air cast for his leg, and Clark was then carted to the locker room .
For the Seahawks, it's the second player they lost to injury this week. During their joint practice with the Titans, they lost wide receiver Jake Bobo to an injury as well. Bobo also had to be carted off, and head coach Mike Macdonald said it was a significant injury .
A second-round pick out of TCU, Clark is currently fighting for his spot on the roster behind starters Ty Okada and Julian Love. When he was initially selected, there were whispers that he could push for a starting role, but Okada has proven to be the better option at this point. That said, Clark was in line for a key role as a rotational piece of their secondary puzzle.
Clark had three tackles in his preseason debut and still needed to hold off players such as A.J. Finley and Rodney Thomas. He was still seen as a more promising overall prospect, especially with the ball-hawking skills he displayed at TCU. NCAA rules allowed Clark to play in a sixth season in 2025, allowing him to play 61 games. He recorded 214 tackles, 21 pass defenses, and 15 interceptions.
Seattle was unable to retain former starting safety Coby Bryant, which opened the door for Okada. Their defensive scheme leans heavily on safeties, however, which is why Clark was expected to see plenty of snaps.
As for the Seahawks' first-round pick, Jadarian Price has yet to suit up. Seattle announced earlier in the day that they wouldn't play Price in the preseason , and this injury helps justify that decision.
We will keep you updated with any developments regarding Clark's injury.

title: Seahawks Announce Surprising Plan for Jadarian Price This Preseason
full_text:
The Seahawks are doing some heavy churn in their backfield this season , with both of their top backs from last season unavailable for different reasons. A lot of the pressure to perform falls on top rookie and first round pick Jadarian Price. However, we won’t be seeing him until the regular season, per Gregg Bell , an interesting decision by the team.
Price has already sat out the team’s mock game at Lumen field and the initial preseason game with vaguely-defined soreness . And according to the article, he won’t be playing tonight against the Titans or next week against the Chiefs. It doesn’t sound like the decision is motivated by any current injury, but rather the possibility of a future injury they want to prevent.
The running back room has already been too thinned by injury to risk the inevitable starter and likely load-bearing back in exhibition games. Furthermore, the team seems to believe that they’ve seen enough of his ability in practice to know he’s good to go. And with the Seahawks already planning to play backups tonight anyway, better safe than sorry.
I can understand the concern, given the Titans have already announced their plans to play starters for some of tonight’s games. They already went at it hard in the joint practice on Friday. Putting Price behind a backup offensive line with backup receivers and backup quarterbacks carries at least some degree of risk. Risk that the team can’t afford to take.
Obviously, Zach Charbonnet is out for the start of the regular season , with his return not yet given a firm timetable yet. Emanuel Wilson has a hamstring injury, and while he’s expected to be back for the start of the regular season, it still leaves the team in a precarious situation. George Holani is the one healthy option expected to make the team.
The Seahawks believe that Price can get all the ramp-up he needs in practice, where the reviews on his play have mostly been excellent . It’s an understandable decision given the above issues with the running back room, but it’s not typical in the NFL. Price was already a backup with limited usage in college, and now he jumps right into the regular season.
The Seahawks open their title defense on September 9th at Lumen Field against the New England Patriots. It’s expected that Price will play a significant role for the team in that game and every game going forward. He’ll certainly have fresh legs when he does it.

title: Did the Seahawks Make a Mistake Gambling at Running Backs?
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks had a tough offseason start, losing key contributors, including Super Bowl MVP and running back Kenneth Walker III. It didn’t help that Zach Charbonnet remains out for a portion of the 2026 season as he recovers from an ACL tear. The Seahawks made the running back position one of the top team priorities this offseason by drafting Jadarian Price with the first-round, 32nd overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
They also took a gamble by betting on third-string back George Holani and former Green Bay Packers backup Emanuel Wilson. All three backs have been tested and inserted into the Seahawks’ system, but there are early signs the gamble is a bad draw. The biggest stress is on Wilson and Holani. It is still too early to worry about Price as his tests come in the regular season.
The Seahawks’ biggest free-agent addition at running back this offseason is a 5-10, 226-pounder who rushed for 496 yards and three touchdowns on 125 carries. He got a bump in carries with Josh Jacobs being injured.
There were concerns about Wilson heading into OTAs, mini-camps and training camps that he would make the Seahawks’ offense limited, as he doesn’t possess the explosiveness or speed to be on the field for non-power plays.
There was also a risk for him with potential injuries. After Price was out with leg soreness , Holani and Wilson took some of the first-team reps. Shortly after, Wilson started dealing with a hamstring injury and didn’t play in the Seahawks’ first preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys.
While Holani and Price continue to split the first-team reps, Wilson doesn’t get the reps or the attention needed. There isn’t an indication from coaches that Wilson will play in the second game against the Tennessee Titans.
One of the biggest attributes Seahawks coaches love about Holani is his work ethic and how he developed as a former undrafted player. He has shown flashes and impressed coaches because the expectations with him were so low, backing up Walker and Charbonnet. Rather than the team getting replacements, the Seahawks took the biggest gamble on Holani to show the team can utilize a group of hard-working running backs.
Holani has looked solid in practices, especially during training camp and preseason. He got one of his biggest tests yet by being the outright first-string running back in the preseason game against the Cowboys last week. While the offensive line didn’t play up to standards, he didn’t have the best results, rushing for 42 yards on 12 carries.
He should be one of the top backs as the Seahawks take on the Tennessee Titans . His performance against the Titans should relieve some stress in the backfield.

title: The Latest on Seattle Seahawks WR Tory Horton's Injury
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have already been tested at the wide receiver position in recent days thanks to the Jake Bobo season-ending injury .
That loss, by itself, wouldn’t really do much to hurt the team, but he’s not the only wounded backup receiver on this team. Tory Horton hasn’t practiced recently, and head coach Mike Macdonald acknowledged he’s working through something on Thursday.
Other than that fact, however, Macdonald kept things quiet. He offered no timetable, or even what’s injured. His secretive nature is understandable, given how things work in the NFL, but is nevertheless frustrating for us fans who might not be sure what to think. Is this just something minor that should be cleared up by the regular season, or something far more serious?
Tory Horton had a cracked tibia last season , which cost him the second half of the year and even some offseason work. That injury was also rather mysterious, starting out as something minor before eventually turning into an ordeal spanning several months. We didn’t get a full picture of what was even going on until fairly recently, in fact. So, we might fear the worst.
The Horton situation combined with Bobo’s injury creates something of a concern at the position as we head towards the regular season. The loss of one player might be just an annoyance, but both? Now you’re pushing into uncomfortable territory. The good news is the Seahawks should be a team that is light at receiver since they use a lot of tight ends and a fullback .
But if Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, or Cooper Kupp get banged up at any point this season, now you’re giving significant snaps to a player who doesn’t have the upside or trust in getting the job done. Let’s assume, for a moment, that Horton will be missing significant time. Who can the Seahawks turn to as the first wideout off the bench?
The hot name in Seattle right now when it comes to backup wideouts is Montorie Foster Jr, who is having a big training camp and had a good first preseason game . I could see him being the one who gets reps in the event of an emergency. Cody White might be the recipient of opportunities as well, given his experience.
The special teams side is worth considering as well, as Bobo and Horton both have significant contributions there. Emmanuel Henderson Jr, a sixth round pick four months ago, was a big special teamer at Kansas , and Irv Charles was a wizard on coverage teams in New York before injuries halted his career. There are options, but hopefully, Horton is back soon.

title: How the Seahawks Can Turn Preseason Around Against the Titans
full_text:
Coming off a Super Bowl win, the Seattle Seahawks had a productive offseason and training camp. The front office answered questions regarding roster holes, and there were players who stepped up this offseason. Since the rough 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys in the first preseason game, the Seahawks had some tough moments. The Seahawks’ second-and-third-string players didn’t have a good performance against Dallas.
That momentum then led to some good, but not great performances in practices. The team saw struggles at key position groups; they had some up-and-down moments in the joint practice against the Tennessee Titans and the Seahawks then lost wide receiver Jake Bobo to a season-ending knee injury. Seattle needs a rebound game against Tennessee to put out the team fires before it heads into the regular season.
The Seahawks were dominated at the line of scrimmage on both sides of the field against the Cowboys. Through the first drives, Seattle looked like the aggressive team that won the Super Bowl, but not long into the game, they were getting pushed at the line of scrimmage.
Offensively, we saw why Christian Haynes continues to be a disappointment considering he was a former third-round pick. Offensive tackles Bobby Hart and Logan Brown showed why they likely shouldn’t be on the Seahawks’ 53-man roster or earn a spot on the practice squad.
The Seahawks’ defensive line struggled to stop the run and create a pass rush. Second-year defensive tackle/end Rylie Mills struggled significantly and edge rushers Jalan Gaines and Jared Ivey struggled to get in the backfield.
Seattle will likely play their starters for a drive or two just to get some real work in, but all groups of the team need to be more consistent at the line of scrimmage. The Seahawks need to protect the quarterback better and have the backups redeem themselves .
The defensive line needs to be more efficient and not get dominated at the line themselves. Seattle allowed Dallas to convert 11-of-15 on third downs. That can’t happen, or players might be cut sooner than expected.
One of the biggest offseason questions for the Seahawks was the need for a No. 3 cornerback after they let Riq Woolen walk to free agency. The front office signed veteran Noah Igbinoghene early in the offseason and drafted Julian Neal in the third round. Head coach Mike Macdonald also challenged third-year cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett to step up.
The competition has left Neal injured for most of training camp, Pritchett starting with the first-team defense and going back to second-string and Igbinoghene taking the lead for the No. 3 cornerback spot. That hasn’t stopped the Seahawks from agreeing to eventually sign former first-round pick Terrion Arnold and signing former two-time Pro-Bowler Trevon Diggs, who is still learning the defense.
Pritchett and Igbinoghene won’t have many chances to separate themselves for the No. 3 cornerback spot. Pritchett needs to show he can play a critical role, especially with nickel Nick Emmanwori still recovering from ankle surgery in July. Igbinoghene needs to prepare for the long battle against Diggs and, possibly, Arnold. Both will have the chance to make a head start against the Titans.​
Preseason game one against the Cowboys showed which role players can step up and potentially earn a roster spot. The Seahawks’ game against the Titans will test which 53-man roster spot players can step up. Linebacker Tyrice Knight will be a go-to after a solid performance against the Cowboys . The Seahawks need more from impact players who are not starters, but are likely to make the regular season.
Mills has to be more consistent than he was against the Cowboys, especially with the large hype he received during the offseason. The Seahawks want to see more than solid route-running and a good catch from second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo. Running back George Holani needs more carries and better blocking to truly judge his progress.
Finally, quarterback Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe, defensive end Mike Morris, rookie safety Bud Clark and linebackers Chazz Surratt and Patrick O’Connell need to show their real potential.

title: Sam Darnold Reveals What Makes Jadarian Price 'Special' After Joint Practice
full_text:
Anytime a team uses a first-round pick on a running back, there will be plenty of skepticism. Often considered one of the easiest positions to replace on offense, running backs don't always get the respect they should when it comes to the draft. Those questions only grow louder when that first-round pick is used on a running back who wasn't the starter for his collegiate team.
That was the case for the Seattle Seahawks this year when they decided to use the 32nd overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft on Jadarian Price out of Notre Dame. While Price has all the tools to be a feature back , he happened to share the field with Jeremiyah Love, who was the third overall pick for the Arizona Cardinals.
In Seattle, Price is vying for the starting spot and is battling with George Holani while Zach Charbonnet recovers from ACL surgery . We have yet to see Price play in an NFL game after he sat out the preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys . If we do see him on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, however, Sam Darnold believes he will prove to be "special."
Following their joint practice with the Titans on Friday, Darnold had plenty of praise for the rookie running back. Darnold especially loved how Price can run between the tackles as well as outside, but also sees him as a threat in the passing game.
"He's a special player," Darnold said via Ari Horton and John Boyle of the Seahawks' official website . "He's a really special player. He brings a different facet to the offense that only a guy like him can bring. Whether it's catching passes out of the backfield, catching screens, running in between the tackles, outside of the tackles, he can really do it all. And I know he's just going to continue to get better and learn."
Price made several grabs during the session, including a big gain during seven-on-sevens. He also ripped off a long run during 11-on-11, which was an encouraging sight after he missed time during camp.
As for his versatility, this should come as no surprise to anyone who watched Price at Notre Dame. While he didn't get many targets as a receiver, he made the most of them as he had 87 yards and two touchdowns on just six receptions in 2025. He also proved to be a weapon on special teams, scoring two touchdowns while averaging 37.5 yards per return on kickoffs .
Price proved to be capable of helping his team in multiple ways at Notre Dame and should do the same with the Seahawks.

title: 4 Seahawks Fighting For a Roster Spot in Preseason Week 2 vs. Titans
full_text:
After facing off with one another in a joint practice on Friday in Nashville, the Seattle Seahawks and Tennessee Titans will take the field for a Preseason Week 2 matchup on Sunday night.
Preseason games might not always be full of excitement, but that doesn't mean there aren't reasons to watch, especially for diehard fans interested in roster construction. While the coaching staff learns plenty during training camp and joint practices, players can still make a strong case for themselves during the preseason.
That's especially true for the following four Seahawks players who will enter Sunday night's meeting with the Titans fighting for their place on the roster.
Signed this offseason as a free agent to give Seattle depth at offensive tackle, Bobby Hart is already in danger of not making the team. Hart hasn't stood out in camp but what really has him feeling the heat is his performance against the Cowboys in Week 1. Hart gave up a sack against James Houston and struggled to slow down rookie Malachi Lawrence.
The one thing that helps him is that Seattle doesn't have anyone else proving to be a vastly superior option, but Hart is definitely entering this game with plenty of weight on his shoulders.
After the Seahawks signed Trevon Diggs, both Nehemiah Pritchett and Noah Igbinoghene find themselves on the roster bubble. Of the two, however, Pritchett might be in the most immediate danger. While Diggs will likely move ahead of each, Seahawks On SI's Jeremy Brener noted that Igbinoghene's work in the slot shields him slightly from Diggs' addition since the former NFL interception leader plays primarily on the outside.
That means Pritchett enters Week 2 of the NFL preseason feeling the pressure. He already finds himself fighting for his spot on the team with players such as rookie third-round pick Julian Neal already ahead of him. This latest addition only makes it tougher for him to find a path to the 53-man roster .
Jadarian Price was expected to be the RB1 this season while Zach Charbonnet recovers from ACL surgery, but George Holani had different plans. Holani was a standout throughout camp and inserted his name into the conversation. The question is whether that remains the case after he averaged just 3.5 yards per attempt against the Cowboys last week. The offensive line did him no favors, but if Holani really wants to hold off Price, he needs a better showing this weekend.
Behind Price and Holani is Emanuel Wilson, who signed with Seattle in the offseason . Wilson has yet to make his debut, but has a chance to see some action on Sunday, assuming he's recovered enough from his hamstring injury. If he does play, he needs to prove he deserves to be in the rotation. If he sits out again, his chance to earn a significant role early in the year could begin to fade.

title: How Does ESPN Rank the Seahawks by Position Group?
full_text:
We’re almost done with the NFL offseason, so any and all offseason-coded content should get pushed out now before it’s too late. Yesterday, ESPN published an article exploring every team’s roster, ultimately ranking every positional group individually. Let’s see how the Seahawks come out here, and sort each ranking into one of three categories
These rankings strike me as appropriate. Wide Receiver at sixth reflects a belief that Rashid Shaheed will take big steps forward this year and produce more in line with what he did in New Orleans, as well as Cooper Kupp possibly having a resurgence after an impressive training camp. EDGE ranking low, but not at the bottom, is also reasonable given the question marks.
The interior defensive line coming in at first is a no-brainer in my mind, and we got a writeup in the article for it as well. Mike Clay gives love to Leonard Williams , Byron Murphy II, and Jarran Reed, as well as their elite run defense, but didn’t mention Rylie Mills. Throw in what he figures to do this season, and Seattle is head and shoulders above anyone else here.
I’m not sure how Sam Darnold can be considered a bottom half of the league starter after two straight successful seasons and a super bowl. And if this list is also supposed to factor in backups, it becomes even more dubious. For some reason, Ernest Jones can’t get any respect this offseason despite making All-Pro, and there’s no love for Knight as a quality backup.
Assuming the safety ranking includes Nick Emmanwori, which I suspect it does, that should be higher as well given how good Julian Love is when healthy, which many have seemingly forgotten. And while I can understand not buying Elijah Arroyo as an impact player yet , A.J. Barner alone should fetch more than the 18th best tight ends in football.
It’s not a huge difference, but between inexperience and injury I feel our running back room is bottom five. The article actually identified running back as a unit to watch, pointing out Price’s inexperience as a pass catcher and Charbonnet’s torn ACL . Given the scrambling the team has done in recent weeks at cornerback, top five seems high there as well.
The offensive line is tricky. I could see the unit as a whole being worthy of the 8th spot, but that’s mostly because of the continuity the group has together. Individually, I don’t think the talent level is quite there, although it’s not far off either. So, it’s all a matter of perspective.

title: 3 Seahawks to Watch vs. Titans in Preseason Clash
full_text:
There are two preseason games left on the schedule for the Seahawks, meaning every single snap is precious and valuable if you’re fighting for a job. If my assumption about this game being a showcase for the backups is correct, for some, this might be the last chance. Let’s talk about three players in particular who need to impress tomorrow.
Probably the most obvious one. Milroe did some good things last week against the Cowboys , but he also did some bad things, and overall showed fairly marginal improvement from last year. If Darnold gets snaps against the Chiefs, as I believe he will, Jalen’s opportunities to make a positive impression will be limited to whatever drives are left after Lock’s time.
That means this Titans game is Milroe’s shot. And it might be the last one, since it’s unlikely he’ll be getting snaps in the regular season, and the upcoming offseason might be an opportunity for the Seahawks to pivot off of him if they’re not impressed. The 2027 draft is rich with quarterbacks , so Jalen needs to give the team a reason to not sniff around in eight months.
The Jake Bobo injury from yesterday’s joint practice has opened the door for another wide receiver to make this team. Based on everything we’ve heard from training camp, Montorie Foster Jr seems like he’s good to go. But that leaves an opening for someone, and while I’d expect Cody White to be the clubhouse leader, the door is open.
Emmanuel Henderson Jr is younger and cheaper than White, and was a special teams whiz in college , so the primary remaining question is whether he can offer something on offense. Make a few plays tomorrow evening, and I could see Henderson jumping the line a bit. Bobo’s main value was on special teams, so getting a rookie who can fill that hole would be big.
I suspect that Morris will make the team, but he is entering the final year of his contract, which makes money a consideration. Mike is built like an interior defensive lineman, but the team already has enough of those, particularly if Brandon Pili makes it . However, the team likes to utilize him as an oversized edge, which is where things become compelling.
The team could use a fifth edge rusher to take a handful of snaps a game, and none of the obvious candidates did much to stand out last week. Morris, however, got into the backfield a couple of times , and if he ends up being the best option, then there may be a role for him yet.

title: What 49ers LBs Warner and Greenlaw Have Instilled in Rookie Jaden Dugger
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers rookie Jaden Dugger has had the privilege of learning from two of the NFL’s most established linebackers in Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw.
The two are the most experienced linebackers on the 49ers’ roster and formed one of the league’s most formidable pairings from 2019 to 2023.
Dugger revealed that he stayed in the Bay Area between the offseason program and the start of training camp to learn the ropes from Warner and Greenlaw, working every day to improve his game and adjust to the NFL standard.
"I just learned so much from them, just what they expect out of certain stuff, just certain techniques, just a lot of stuff," Dugger told reporters on Saturday .
"Just picking up stuff from those vets, and the two best linebackers, so it's been good for me.
"Really, the approach to the game, that's what's the most important—being relentless, running to the ball all the time.
"If you watch film, you're going to see those guys running to the ball all the time. That's like the Forty-Niner way.
"You're taught that in college, but they don't harp on it as much. But now, when you come here, that's the standard. In practice, even if you're 40 yards away, you go chase the ball.
"So, just watching those guys and watching the team in general, just the culture around here, just that's what it taught me."
It deserves respect that Dugger decided to stay in the area to learn and understand more before training camp.
Being a rookie means everything is brand new, but using the opportunity to learn from Warner and Greenlaw is the perfect way to gain familiarity with the scheme and the very high standards they set within the organization.
How much Dugger will be seen on the field during his rookie season remains to be seen. But it's realistic that his first-year contributions could be primarily on special teams and in a rotational role on defense.
That way he can continue developing without being asked to shoulder too much responsibility right away. After all, he's doing and learning various jobs that could be important later on in the season if injuries hit.
He played nine special-teams snaps against the Los Angeles Chargers in the second preseason game, while also making his presence felt defensively with two solo tackles and a pass breakup. So there's plenty of optimism.

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey Puts To Bed All Hold-In Narratives
full_text:
Rumors about Christian McCaffrey holding out for a pay rise with the San Francisco 49ers have now been put to bed.
McCaffrey had been away from training camp for several days, and without any further context, his absence looked worrying on paper.
The reason given was simply “tightness,” with no elaboration on where or how serious it was. When head coach Kyle Shanahan was pressed for more information, he didn’t want to reveal much more, so naturally, speculation began to swirl.
A key theme throughout this offseason has always centred around the 49ers being careful with McCaffrey’s workload . It’s a point that has been emphasised time and time again.
The 49ers cannot afford an injury to McCaffrey or for him to miss significant game time. He played every single game last season and was hugely influential in San Francisco defying the odds to make the playoffs despite a heavily injured roster.
He remains the focal point of the offense, with much of the 49ers’ game plan built around him and his attributes, even though last season saw him lose some of the explosiveness that has defined his career.
Thankfully, at least for now, McCaffrey has put those concerns to rest, explaining that his absence was more about preparing for the Week 1 season opener in Australia than anything related to his contract.
“Yeah obviously when you don’t practice, the way the media works now it’s a firestorm," McCaffrey told reporters on Sunday .
"But this was part of the plan from the jump was to ramp up pretty big, get 9 or 10 practices in, kind of come back down and then ramp back up so we’re fresh for the duration.
"Our staff's done a great job of coming up with specific plans. Again, I feel great. I feel fresh, and it’s good to be back out there.”
A key point with McCaffrey is that he enters this season in much better physical shape than he did 12 months ago, when he was coming off a disastrous 2024 campaign that limited him to just four games.
San Francisco now need to keep their promise of carefully managing his workload, because freshness could define his season. There are plenty of people who believe McCaffrey has lost the explosiveness that once made him so dangerous, but his improved health compared to a year ago offers plenty of reason for optimism that we could see more glimpses of his 2022 and 2023 self.

title: The Case For and Against the 49ers Playing George Kittle Week 1
full_text:
Sunday, August 23, is a pivotal moment for San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle.
The 49ers announced they had activated Kittle from the Active/Physically Unable to Perform List.
He took part in certain individual drills but wasn't participating in team drills, which is the right move, as slowly easing him back in makes sense. But prior to the 49ers activating him, Kittle had been doing solo drills away from the roster during training camp, so think of this as the next step.
It’s absolutely admirable that Kittle is out there and looks to be in fine shape. But is he fully 100%? Or is he at 80% and just easing back into it?
If he feels anything other than 100%, making the 16-hour flight to face the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Week 1 wouldn’t make any sense.
Kittle’s rehab to be in this position has been nothing short of miraculous, and he deserves every bit of credit. But the last thing the 49ers need is a reinjury or a setback in his recovery.
It’s Week 1. As Kittle rightfully called playing in Australia a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity , risking him in the season opener simply isn’t worth it if he’s not 100%. The recovery period between Week 1 and Week 2 provides the perfect buffer for Kittle to continue building himself back up and potentially be ready for San Francisco’s Week 2 game at Levi’s Stadium.
Every encouraging update makes it look more and more likely that Kittle will actually be 100% in time for the trip. The 49ers will be flying out on September 2, more than a week before the season opener.
That gives Kittle additional time to prove he can handle an increased workload in practice before the team has to make a decision on his availability.
If Kittle continues progressing without any setbacks and starts participating in team drills, then the conversation changes significantly. There would be far more reason for the 49ers to feel comfortable putting him on that flight.
Nobody should expect the 49ers to take an unnecessary gamble, but if Kittle is genuinely 100% and receives full medical clearance, there’s little reason to hold him back from an opportunity he clearly wants to be part of.
It's a tough choice to make. Let's see what happens in the next week.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 16 of 49ers Camp: Kittle and McCaffrey Return
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just finished Day 16 of training camp. Here's who stood out.
Practiced for the first time since he tore his Achilles in January. Participated in individual drills with the other tight ends but did not participate in 1-on-1 or 11-on-11 team drills, which are dangerous. The 49ers are smart to go slow with Kittle, considering he's way ahead of schedule. I expect he will fly to Australia and play against the Rams in Week 1. I don't think he'll dominate as he has in the past, but I think he'll help, and I think the 49ers will win. Call me a homer.
He must be worried about Kittle taking all of his playing time, because in the past two practices, Tonges has gone crazy. Today, he caught a team-high six passes. He was Brock Purdy's go-to guy, particularly after Mike Evans went down for the third time in camp (more on him in a minute). After Evans left the field, the 49ers started using lots of tight ends. I've never seen them do this before. Hopefully, they'll do it during the season with Kittle, Tonges and Luke Farrell.
Practiced for the first time in two weeks and looked fresh and ready for Week 1. Unlike Kittle, McCaffrey participated in team drills with no restrictions. He seems poised to have a good year, particularly because the 49ers seem intent on resting him at times. They really like Kaelon Black.
Caught two passes from Purdy in the first three plays of 11-on-11s. Black isn't a hybrid slot receiver like McCaffrey, but he can catch passes, and the 49ers will throw to him. He's a three-down player. But the best thing he does is run the ball, particularly between the tackles. He has the speed to get to the perimeter, but he wants to run downhill. He hits holes between the tackles with zero hesitation, and can squirt through the tiniest of creases. In that sense, he reminds me of Frank Gore. At one point, he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Fred Warner on a pass over the middle, stayed down for a second, shook his head, ran back to the huddle, lined up in the backfield, took the handoff and exploded around the left side for a 20-yard gain. He's so tough.
Returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. Wore a black non-contact jersey but still participated fully and even caught a 15-yard pass near the sideline from Purdy while being covered by Jack Jones.
Also returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. At one point, he even lined up in the slot as a nickelback, something I haven't seen him do in two years. Wherever he lines up, Purdy usually stays away from him.
Intercepted Purdy while covering Stribling in the slot. Stribling ran a dig route over the middle, Purdy released the pass before Stribling turned his head, and Stout broke on the pass before Stribling knew it was coming his way. Stout and Lenoir are by far the best players in the 49ers' secondary. The rest of the starters are shaky.
Intercepted Mac Jones on a pass over the middle that was intended for Jacob Cowing. Davis is nearly 30 years old, and he hasn't had much success playing safety in his career, but he just might be good enough to start for the 49ers, considering their starting free safety, Marques Sigle, almost never makes plays on the ball. And today, he blew his assignment in the middle of the field and gave up an uncontested 70-yard touchdown catch to Jordan Watkins. Give Davis a chance.
Broke up two passes -- a deep one intended for Will Pauling, and a short one intended for Malik Turner. It's just a matter of time before Prysock joins Lenoir and Stout as starters in the secondary. He has incredible athletic gifts, he doesn't give up much separation, and he makes plays on the ball. What more could you want?
Broke up and nearly intercepted a pass from Purdy over the middle that was intended for Evans. Greenlaw hasn't made a ton of plays in camp, and he frequently comes off the field in clear passing situations such as third down. But on this play, he nearly made a one-handed interception. Still, I wonder about his ability to break down and change directions after tearing his Achilles. Don't expect him to be a full-time player this year.
He's probably the second-best defensive tackle on the team after Osa Odighizuwa. Thompson Jr. is a terrific run defender who actually can rush the passer as well. Today, he lined up with the starters and beat Carver Willis to "sack" Purdy. Whoever scouted this guy deserves a promotion.
Left practice early yet again. A few days ago, he left the joint practice against the Chargers early due to a quad strain. This injury doesn't appear serious, and yet Evans can't make it through consecutive practices without reaggravating it. Today, he ran a deep corner route, which required him to sprint, he pulled up at the end of the play, took off his shoulder pads and watched the rest of practice from the sideline. He just doesn't seem like he's going to make it through the entire season. I wouldn't be surprised if he starts some games he doesn't finish. No wonder the 49ers are breaking out their three-tight-end formations. Practically all of their wide receivers are banged up.
Hasn't practiced in more than three weeks. Didn't even show up to watch practice from the sideline. Either he's extremely unhappy with his contract and is holding in for an extension, or his knee tendinitis is worse than the 49ers have let on. If he plays Week 1, it's fair to wonder how effective he'll be. He probably won't be in football shape, and new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris might not know how to use him. And without Bosa, the 49ers defense is in serious trouble. I don't think Morris has the chops to build a viable defense without his only effective edge rusher.
Missed practice with an undisclosed injury. Which means both of the 49ers' primary edge rushers are injured. Not to mention Mykel Williams, their first-round pick from last year, who seems months away from returning from a torn ACL. I don't see how the defense can be good without a legitimate edge rush.
Nearly knocked out Kaelon Black with a vicious helmet-to-helmet hit. Remember, Warner knocked out Renardo Green from the joint practice against the Chargers a few days ago, and knocked out Jordan James for three weeks after punching him when he wasn't wearing pads and breaking his ribs. Warner has been out of control all of camp. And he has been loud, too. You frequently can hear him taunting the offense. So today, Purdy completed a pass right over Warner's head, then immediately screamed an obscenity at Warner. I didn't know Purdy uses words like that. Afterward, Warner walked over to Purdy and they appeared to hash things out.
He's trying to install so many new things, and he doesn't currently have the personnel to pull off any of them. To be fair, his players do a good job aggressively breaking on intermediate passes over the middle, but they can't seem to stop anything else. Today, Morris kept using a defense with five defensive linemen, one linebacker and five defensive backs. And it couldn't stop anything -- not the run or the pass. On third down, he wants to be aggressive and blitz. This just leaves his subpar safeties one on one against superior players. And if the blitz doesn't get to the quarterback right away, which it usually doesn't, the defense gives up huge catches. I have a feeling this defense will struggle big time this season.

title: 5 Major Questions the 49ers Must Answer Before Cutdowns
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers enter the last week of practice before roster cutdowns , what are the biggest questions facing the team?
Stribling has been one of the most impactful rookies of the preseason . The only question now is how often he plays and in what role? The team has been resting Mike Evans, but it is notable that Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson started at wide receiver in two wide-out sets in the second preseason. Those two were held out in the preseason opener with the starters.
Stribling had a hot preseason but might be a rotational player early in his career.
The left guard battle might end up with a winner by default. Connor Colby appears to have bowed out after moving over to right guard for the past few weeks. Robert Jones has been banged up and has not taken over the job. Austen Pleasants looked unfamiliar with left guard.
Meanwhile, rookie Carver Willis got work with the first team last week and started in front of Brock Purdy in the preseason game. Did he just win the job?
The backup center job could end up being resolved soon. Brett Toth was signed to take on the role, but he has not been healthy enough to take it. Third-year UDFA Drake Nugent has taken snaps once again and appears to be going from practice squad lock to backup center. Can he finalize winning the job?
The 49ers have investments in Osa Odighizuwa, Alfred Collins, Gracen Halton, and C.J. West. However, three of the best stories in training camp are Sebastian Valdez, James Thompson, and Bryson Eason.
All three have bottom-of-the-roster potential with practice squad lock ability. Can they keep all three around in some manner?
The 49ers signed Vederian Lowe to be their backup left tackle. He started the year on PUP, returned, and immediately got hurt . Austen Pleasants has held the job down with Lowe out. Does Lowe return, do they ride with Pleasants, or does rookie Enrique Cruz sneak into the mix?

title: It’s Hard to Argue With this ‘Expiration Date’ Take on the 49ers
full_text:
Is time running out for this current San Francisco 49ers core to finally win a Super Bowl?
It’s the dreaded question. It’s one that San Francisco won’t be able to avoid unless they win it all with this current core, who have reached multiple NFC Championship Games and come up short twice in the Super Bowl.
The Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era reaches double figures this season, so naturally, much of the core built during their earlier years, with Brock Purdy being the obvious exception , are now in their late 20s or early 30s. Time is beginning to run out for several key players who are entering, or could already be past, their primes.
"The fact that they continue to be contenders with this aging roster, that they haven't dramatically retooled, I think it's delaying the retooling, and there's going to be a point where they just have to do a massive overhaul and not hang on to this guy one more year because maybe we can get over the hump," discussed Mike Florio and Michael Holley on their show .
"They're still, for the most part, other than the quarterback position, it's gone from Jimmy Garoppolo to Brock Purdy, but this feels like a team that's had its soul constructed away from the quarterback position, the George Kittles of the world, the Nick Bosas, the Fred Warners, the Dre Greenlaws, and it just feels like the expiration date is coming for all of them."
And in truth, it’s not wrong. There’s plenty of skepticism surrounding this team heading into the coming season. Add in free agent Mike Evans, who is now 33 and coming off a bad 2025 , and this season, perhaps alongside 2027, could represent the final true attempts to win with this current core.
It’s clear the 49ers are putting their chips in, but more notably, they’re not sacrificing significant draft capital for future seasons. That suggests they understand a rebuild, or at least a major retooling, is coming when these veterans either decline further, retire or move on.
The far-from-ideal outcome is that this roster could always be remembered as one of the most talented to never get it done. However, there are some names, namely George Kittle and Fred Warner , who will likely remain with the franchise until the end of their careers and go down as one-team players.
Sooner rather than later, the next era of the 49ers will have to be prioritized. The question is when the 49ers’ front office will decide it’s time to make that call.

title: 5 Injuries that Could Reshape the 49ers' Roster Plans
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are now one week away from the 53-man roster deadline . While they will provide clarity on who makes the team, a few injury situations that are currently unclear might determine how the 49ers roster is sorted out.
Which are the most important injury statuses to watch, as they could impact who makes the roster?
Kittle will be the biggest one to watch between now and the start of the season. All indications are that if Kittle does not return in Week 1, he will be back shortly after. He is currently on the PUP, but if he enters the season on the PUP, he will have to miss six games. The 49ers do not plan on him missing that many games.
So, when will they activate him? More than that, if he is activated and not available for Week 1, do the 49ers have to carry an extra tight end? They cannot go into Week 1 with Jake Tonges and Luke Farrell as their only healthy tight ends.
If a fourth tight end makes the team, it takes away from another position group, though.
Mykel Williams is on the PUP, and his status for Week 1 appears to be even more in doubt. The 49ers have a much tougher debate to leave Williams on the PUP, considering the timing and severity of his injury. Still, without Williams, the team has Nick Bosa, who has been eased back from an injury, rookie Romello Height, Keion White, who is coming back from injury, and depth piece Sam Okuayinonu.
If he is out, Okuayinonu becomes a roster lock, and they might want to add one more player.
Hobbs has a strained groin. He is expected to miss a couple of weeks. Still, he has hardly practiced all summer and is already new to the team. He was activated, so he would have to be placed on IR with a designation to return if he is not on the initial 53-man roster.
James has fractured ribs, and his timeline to return is unclear. He is another IR with a designation to return candidate if he cannot get back soon. Still, without him, the team is thin at running back, and someone like Sincere McCormick might sneak onto the roster.
Lowe came off the PUP and immediately sprained his ankle. Neither Austen Pleasants nor Enrique Cruz made him expendable when he was out. If Lowe is ready for Week 1, one of those two will likely get cut. If not, they have to find a way to get all three onto the roster. It could mean IR with designation to return for Lowe.

title: The 49ers Can Relax Knowing Their Special Teams Are in Good Hands
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers can relax knowing their special teams unit is operating well in preseason.
Special teams can often be overlooked during the preseason because all eyes are on the draft picks. But San Francisco made several changes during the offseason.
Punter Thomas Morstead left to make way for Corliss Waitman, and the 49ers re-signed Jon Weeks and handed Eddy Piñeiro a four-year extension .
It was a strange move to see them let Skyy Moore go to the Green Bay Packers, but at least they retained Luke Gifford on a two-year contract.
Piñeiro has picked up where he left off last season, converting four field-goal attempts against the Tennessee Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers, including 48- and 45-yard kicks against the latter. This is hardly a surprise when you consider his near-perfect conversion rate since joining San Francisco last year.
Though Moore moved on, wide receiver Jacob Cowing has been competing for the return role and made his case with an impressive 83-yard punt return for a touchdown against the Chargers. After missing the entire 2025 season, Cowing looks determined to make an impact wherever possible and strengthen his case for a spot on the final 53-man roster.
The coverage unit also made its mark. Linebacker Nick Martin forced a fumble on kickoff coverage, which KhaDarel Hodge recovered. Just two plays later, the offense took advantage of the excellent field position, with Jordan Watkins hauling in a 17-yard touchdown pass.
There had also been competition at punter, with Waitman battling undrafted rookie Jack Bouwmeester throughout camp. However, Bouwmeester was waived a couple of weeks ago, leaving Waitman as the only punter remaining on the roster.
Despite a handful of changes during the offseason and training camp, the 49ers appear to be in a strong position heading into the regular season.
Plenty of credit should go to special teams coordinator Brant Boyer, who has transformed the unit since arriving in San Francisco in 2025. The early preseason performances suggest his group is continuing to move in the right direction.
For me, special teams were a key reason the 49ers managed to reach the playoffs last season, providing much-needed stability considering the revolving door of injuries across the roster. It’s important to have this aspect of the game as sharp as possible, particularly in a sport as variable and situational as football.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 15 of 49ers Camp: Stribling Injures Shoulder
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just finished Day 15 of training camp. Here's who stood out. Keep in mind, De'Zhaun Stribling missed practice with a shoulder injury. More on him in a minute.
Practiced for the first time since Fred Warner broke his rib on Day 1 of training camp, and looked good. He even ran for a touchdown from 10 yards out. James clearly has fresh legs because he hasn't played in weeks, and he's going to make this team. He might not play much early in the season, but he'll be the third running back on the depth chart behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black.
Has become the unquestioned starting running back since Christian McCaffrey went down with "tightness." For all we know, he could be in Germany right now. Meanwhile, Black is in peak condition, he's extremely decisive when it comes to hitting the hole and he's the fastest running back on the team (Isaac Guerendo doesn't count, more on him in a minute). If McCaffrey were to miss an extended stretch of games this season, the 49ers should be fine without him now that they have Black and James.
Returned to practice after missing the second half of the joint session against the Chargers with a quad injury. When Evans runs, he seems like he's in pain. Maybe that's just how he runs. He still finds a way to catch the ball most of the time. He's a monster in the red zone. Today, Jack Jones had to trip him in the end zone to prevent him from catching a second touchdown pass on the day.
Leapfrogged Deebo Samuel on the depth chart to replace De'Zhaun Stribling in the starting lineup. Which is good news, because Watkins is young and ascending while Samuel is old and declining, and Demarcus Robinson never has been someone teams had to worry about. Today, he dropped a pass that hit him in the chest, while Watkins caught a pass that slipped through the hands of Ji'Ayir Brown (more on him in a minute). If Watkins can catch the ball consistently, he'll become a starting wide receiver. He's an outstanding athlete.
Made some nice catches while playing with the second- and third-stringers. Caught no passes while playing with the starters, but he did run a couple times for minimal gains. The 49ers don't need to use Samuel at running back anymore now that they have Black and James, and they don't need to use him at wide receiver either now that they have Evans, Stribling and Watkins. They also don't need to use him as a punt returner now that Jacob Cowing has asserted himself. Of course, the 49ers will find ways to use Samuel even though they have better players, and that's what makes him special.
Caught two 25-yard passes near the sideline. Cowing's confidence seems to be growing. He just needs to stay healthy for longer than a week a time.
The unquestioned MVP of practice. He beat Jaden Dugger up the seam for a gain of 20, then he beat Dre Greenlaw on a wheel route for a 70-yard touchdown, then he beat Marques Sigle with an over route for another gain of 20. Tonges is a legit matchup problem against most linebackers and lots of safeties, particularly the ones on the 49ers. He should catch at least 40 passes this season.
At 6-6, 310 pounds, he's the player the 49ers wanted Alfred Collins to be. Unlike Collins, Thompson can anchor and hold his ground against double-teams in the run game, plus he can push the pocket, get off blocks and make plays in the backfield. As opposed to Collins (more on him in a minute). Thompson Jr. is an undrafted rookie, and he absolutely should make the team. He might even become a starter soon. He's that good at what he does.
Missed practice with a shoulder injury he apparently suffered Thursday during the 49ers' preseason game against the Chargers. Showed up to practice and watched with the other wide receivers, so it seems his injury isn't serious. He doesn't seem to need surgery or anything drastic. I'm guessing he'll miss the final preseason game, which is fine, considering he doesn't need to play anymore in the preseason, anyway. He has shown enough. The 49ers need him healthy for Week 1, and I expect he will be.
Also missed practice with a shoulder injury. Lenoir has missed just two games in the past four seasons -- he has been the iron man of the secondary. Without him, the 49ers have no defensive backs who scare anyone. Heal up quickly, Deommodore.
Missed practice with a hamstring injury he suffered two days ago against the Chargers. Don't be surprised if this injury keeps him out of Week 1. The 49ers love his backup, Jack Jones.
Got worked left and right by Mike Evans. The only time Evans didn't beat him was when Jones tripped him. For some reason, the 49ers are convinced that Jones is good, even though three teams already have gotten rid of him. If he starts Week 1, I predict he'll get benched by halftime.
Started at cornerback in place of Renardo Green and immediately gave up a 15-yard catch to Evans. I can't remember Luter ever breaking up a pass, let alone intercepting one in practice. I'm sure he has, but he probably did so a long time ago. He's one of the worst players on the team.
Let a potential interception fly right through his hands and land in the arms of Jordan Watkins for a gain of 30. Brown is entering his fourth season in the league, and he's still not good.
Plays exclusively with the starters and makes no impact as a pass rusher. I'm not sure what he has done to earn a starting job, but they've given it to him, probably because they drafted him in Round 3 and they don't have many quality edge rushers on the roster. Nick Bosa can't come back fast enough.
Got moved out of his gap repeatedly by double teams on run plays. Collins is the rare big defensive tackle who's bad against the run and generates no push in the pocket. The 49ers should trade him while he still has value, if he still has value.
It doesn't do anything well right now. Maybe that's because it has a new defensive coordinator. Maybe it's because he wants to do so much. Every play, they have a different front. Sometimes they go with a five-man front with base personnel. Other times they go with a four-man front from base personnel. Other times they use a five-man front with nickel personnel. Other times they use a four-man front with nickel personnel. It seems like Morris is searching for something that works and finding nothing.
Brock Purdy had his moments, but also threw a pass right to Ji'Ayir Brown, then sailed four passes over the heads of his intended receivers. When Purdy misses, he tends to miss high. When Mac Jones misses in practice, he tends to get intercepted. Today, he got picked by Eli Apple after throwing a quick slant to Evans, who was late coming out of his break.
Still recovering from a torn pec. I get the feeling he's going to spend the entire season on I.R., just because the 49ers don't think highly of him. I'm guessing he has played his last snap with this team.
